new_roles.title: Quality Director
new_roles.description:
**Build Your Career. Lead With Precision.**

Nammo Perry is a center of excellence for the design, development and production of munitions and pyrotechnic products for the U.S. Department of Defense. Nammo employees working at the Florida site manufacture all types of 40mm low and high velocity ammunition; pyrotechnic marking; signaling and tactical illumination devices; battlefield effects training simulators; demolition charges; hand grenade fuzes; and other ammunition components. Additionally, they provide load, assemble, and pack (LAP) services for large caliber direct-fire ammunition.

The **Director of Quality** provides strategic leadership and oversight of quality assurance, quality systems, supplier quality, and configuration management across Nammo Perry supporting the Large Caliber Systems and Aerospace Propulsion business units. Reporting to the President/General Manager, this position leads a multidisciplinary quality organization through four direct-report management functions: Configuration Management, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality Systems, and Quality Assurance. These functions collectively support supplier compliance, product conformity, manufacturing qualities, inspection and testing, calibration, customer quality, and configuration controls.

The Director is accountable for establishing and maintaining a robust quality management system (QMS), ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry requirements, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization. A key strategic priority is leading the site's transformation from ISO9001 certification to AS9100 certification encompassing both business units under one unified quality management system, as well as a robust supplier quality program.

**Unique Benefits Designed with Care**

* Monday - Thursday work week working 10-hour days
* Relocation assistance provided
* 401(K) with a 6% company match
* 100% Employer-Paid Employee Only Medical Plan Option
* Employer Health Saving Account Contributions
* Two week’s vacation, one-week sick pay, and nine paid holidays

**What You’ll Do: Precision in Action**

**Strategic Quality Leadership**

* Develop and execute quality strategies aligned with organizational objectives, customer requirements, regulatory expectations, and long-term business growth.
* Provide leadership and accountability across configuration management, supplier quality systems, and quality assurance ensuring consistent quality standards across both business units.
* Monitor key performance indicators related to product conformity, supplier performance, customer satisfaction, cost of poor quality, and continuous improvement.
* Partner with site leadership to evaluate quality risks, organizational capabilities, resource allocation, and strategic improvement opportunities.

**Quality Management Systems**

* Maintain compliance with existing ISO9001 and AS9100requirements while continuing to foster an environment of continuous improvement.
* Provides strategic oversight of the Quality Systems Organization including internal audits, corrective and preventative actions, document control, calibration, and customer quality activities.
* Ensure effective management review processes, regulatory and customer audit readiness, and continuous improvement of quality systems and organizational performance.

**Supplier Quality and Configuration Management**

* Provide strategic oversight of Supplier Quality including supplier qualification, performance monitoring and auditing, incoming inspection, and supplier corrective action processes.
* Ensure supplier quality engineering and receiving inspection activities support material conformity traceability and manufacturing readiness
* Lead Configuration Management functions to ensure appropriate control of product configuration, engineering changes, technical documentation, and applicable customer requirements through the established configuration management and business systems.
* Partner with supply chain engineering and operations to manage supplier risk, resolve quality concerns, and maintain effective configuration and product controls.

**Manufacturing Quality Assurance and Testing**

* Provide leadership and oversight of the Quality Assurance organization supporting manufacturing quality, engineering inspection, and testing activities across both business units.
* Support integrated product teams by offer subject expertise, ensuring programmatic needs are met
* Ensure effective execution of product inspection verification testing and acceptance processes in accordance with applicable specifications and customer requirements.
* Oversee quality assurance capabilities including quality technicians, testing personnel, and specialized inspection activities.
* Drive continuous improvement throughout the organization using established lean six sigma tools.
* Partner with operations and engineering to address manufacturing nonconformances, implement corrective action, and improve process capability and product reliability.

**Compliance, Financial Performance, and People Leadership**

* Ensure compliance with applicable aerospace and defense quality standards, contractual requirements, customer specifications, and regulatory obligations.
* Develop and maintain quality budgets, departmental resources, and improvement initiatives while promoting cost effectiveness and operational efficiency.
* Lead, coach, and develop direct-report managers while establishing clear expectations for performance accountability and organizational effectiveness
* Partner with people and culture on workforce planning succession planning leadership development and employee engagement.

**What Dedicated Teammates Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, or related technical field. Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in quality assurance, quality engineering, quality systems, or quality leadership within a manufacturing environment.
* Minimum of 5 years of management experience including demonstrated success leading managers or multidisciplinary quality teams.
* Experience in aerospace defense, energetic materials, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience implementing, maintaining, or leading quality management systems aligned with ISO9001 and AS9100 requirements.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing, quality supplier, quality configuration management, inspection, testing, and regulatory compliance.
* Proven ability to develop quality strategies, manage budgets, lead organizational change, and drive measurable performance improvements.
* Strong leadership communication, analytical, problem solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

*Preferred Qualifications:*

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Business Administration, or related discipline.
* Direct experience in defense manufacturing, energetic material processing, ammunition production, or aerospace propulsion.
* Demonstrated experience leading an organization through initial AS9100 certification or significant QMS expansion.
* Professional certifications such as ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA).
* Experience with specialized inspection and testing methods, non-destructive testing, and manufacturing process qualifications.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and structured continuous improvement methodologies.

*Leadership Competencies:*

* Aligns operational capabilities and resources with business objectives and long-term growth.
* Drives performance improvements in safety, quality, delivery cost, and reliability.
* Build strong management teams and promotes accountability, engagement, and succession readiness.
* Demonstrate sound judgment, hazard awareness, and commitment to disciplined operations,
* Build effective partnerships across departments and business units
* Leads teams through expansion, organizational growth, and evolving operational requirements.

**Our Woking Conditions and Requirements**

* This position operates in both office and industrial manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with production areas, maintenance, operations, and facility infrastructure.
* The role may involve prolonged periods of sitting, standing, and walking, including navigating manufacturing facilities and operational work areas.
* Employees must comply with applicable safety, security, and environmental requirements including the use of required personal protective equipment (PPE) when entering designated areas.
* The position may require occasional domestic or international travel and flexibility to support operational needs outside standard business hours.
* Must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

*Our values are the fundamental principles guiding the way we do business and interact with stakeholders.*

***DEDICATION:*** *We are enthusiastic and creative, always searching for the best solutions.* 
***PRECISION:*** *We are reliable and accurate in our technology, processes and business.* 
***CARE:*** *We are inclusive and open-minded, always encouraging team spirit and cooperation.*

*Nammo and its subsidiaries provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.*

*This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.*

**\*\*Note\*\*: Due to US Export Control laws and regulations; applicants selected for employment must show proof of a U.S. Person status before employment may begin.**

new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager – Manufacturing**

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead an established, mid-size manufacturing operation in Holt, Michigan. This is an opportunity for a well-rounded manufacturing leader to take ownership of the facility's overall business performance, providing strategic direction and leadership while driving operational excellence, profitability, and continued growth.

Reporting to the VP of Operations, the Plant Manager will have full responsibility for the facility's operational and financial performance, including full P&L accountability. This individual will oversee all aspects of the business, lead and develop the management team, and ensure the facility consistently achieves its financial, operational, quality, safety, and customer objectives.

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a seasoned manufacturing leader who understands how to run a plant as a business. The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of operational expertise, financial acumen, and business leadership, with a proven ability to translate company objectives into measurable results.

This person will be comfortable leading through department managers, establishing accountability, making sound business decisions, and developing a culture of continuous improvement. Equally important is the ability to balance the bigger picture with an understanding of what is happening on the plant floor.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Assume full ownership and accountability for the facility's overall performance, including P&L, profitability, operating costs, and financial results.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, and business strategies aligned with company objectives.
* Monitor financial and operational performance, analyze results, identify areas of opportunity, and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Provide leadership and oversight across all plant functions, including production, quality, maintenance, materials, shipping, and safety.
* Lead, mentor, and develop the management team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Provide direction and oversight to the Production Manager and other functional leaders, ensuring alignment across departments and consistent execution of business objectives.
* Drive improvements in productivity, labor efficiency, throughput, quality, on-time delivery, and overall operating costs.
* Identify and implement cost-reduction initiatives, process improvements, and operational efficiencies that positively impact the bottom line.
* Maintain strong customer relationships, ensuring customer requirements are met and issues are addressed promptly and effectively.
* Oversee workforce planning, staffing, employee development, and organizational effectiveness.
* Ensure a safe working environment and maintain compliance with applicable safety regulations, quality standards, and other requirements.
* Direct capital planning and investment decisions, evaluating equipment, technology, and facility improvements to support business needs and long-term growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators, using data and financial reporting to measure results and drive continuous improvement.
* Partner with senior leadership to communicate facility performance, address business challenges, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success managing an entire plant or manufacturing operation.
* Previous full P&L responsibility, including budgeting, financial reporting, cost management, and profitability.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations, including production, quality, maintenance, materials management, and supporting functions.
* Proven ability to improve financial and operational performance through effective planning, execution, and accountability.
* Experience leading and developing department managers and supervisors, with the ability to build a strong, effective leadership team.
* Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand financial statements, evaluate operating costs, and make sound business decisions.

new_roles.title: Director Internal Fill Finish Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Greenbush
* Req ID:R52954
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. Regeneron is currently looking for a Director of Internal Fill Finish Manufacturing to join our Industrial Operations and Product Supply (IOPS) team. This leadership role is accountable for the aseptic filling operation for clinical and commercial drug products, including vials and syringes in both liquid and lyophilized formats. The Director owns the full filling value stream: materials management; preparation of equipment, format parts, and components; formulation of drug product and placebo; aseptic filling; and lyophilization. The Director also ensures a seamless handoff to downstream finishing operations (Visual Inspection, syringe safety systems and autoinjector assembly, packaging, labeling, and serialization) and oversees facility cleaning and contamination control for the filling suites.

This role focuses on the start-up and execution of compliant GMP aseptic operations, ensuring the facility is properly staffed and trained, and supporting a dynamic, flexible production planning process that meets the needs of Regeneron’s patients. The Director will work directly with Drug Substance and Finish manufacturing management to ensure production timelines are met and will be a key member of various management teams within IOPS.

This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.

**When & where:**

* Location: Rensselaer, NY
* Work model: Monday- Friday, 8am-4:30pm

**Discover your role:**

* Provides leadership, vision, and management to the Filling team and its supporting functions, and leads all aspects of Filling operations at the facility to manufacture commercial and clinical parenteral medicines according to approved protocols, regulations, and schedules
* Directly oversees aseptic filling of drug product and placebo into vials and syringes, in liquid and lyophilized formats, including stoppering, capping, and crimping
* Directly oversees formulation of bulk drug product and placebo, including solution preparation and sterile filtration
* Directly oversees preparation of equipment, format parts, and components to support aseptic filling, including washing, depyrogenation, sterilization, and setup of filling lines
* Directly oversees lyophilization operations, including loading, cycle execution, and unloading, as well as the management of materials and components required to support filling operations
* Directly oversees cleaning and sanitization of filling suites, including Graded space (Grade A–D) and Controlled Non-Classified rooms (iCNC), and supports the site contamination control strategy, environmental monitoring, and aseptic process simulations (media fills)
* Ensures a smooth, timely handoff of filled product to downstream finishing operations (Visual Inspection, assembly, packaging, and labeling) in partnership with the leaders of those areas
* Troubleshoots and resolves issues impeding filling deliverables, including equipment performance, line interventions, and yield; provides technical input to resolve filling and aseptic process challenges
* Partners with department Directors and Project Management to implement new filling processes, including new formats, PFS and vial filling lines, formulation, aseptic filling, and lyophilization
* Manages department metrics and goals, monitors performance to objectives, and drives continuous improvement initiatives essential to meeting patient and business needs
* Leads the annual merit performance review process, builds departmental structure, and develops long-term staffing plans, including aseptic gowning qualification and training programs
* Collaborates with department Directors to support development of the annual budget, and rapidly and accurately communicates issues to department Directors
* Writes, reviews, and/or approves Standard Operating Procedures, specifications, regulatory filings, or other controlled documents as needed
* Executes Quality Management System assignments (CAPA, Deviation, Investigation, Change Control, etc.)
* Participates in the development and maintenance of a safe manufacturing environment and ensures that IOPS safety standards are maintained
* Oversees, supports, and participates in cGMP audits of all filling areas within the facility; maintains site inspection readiness and represents the filling operation during regulatory and client audits

**This role requires:**

* BS in any of the physical or biological sciences or chemical engineering, with biopharmaceutical/biotech experience in a GMP drug product production facility, including aseptic filling experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
 + Director: 12+ years of experience
 + Senior Director: 15+ years of experience
 + Level will be determined based on experience
* Experience overseeing aseptic filling operations in a biologics manufacturing environment, including vial and prefilled syringe filling
* Working knowledge of lyophilization, formulation, and aseptic technique, including barrier and isolator/RABS technologies
* Working knowledge of contamination control, environmental monitoring, and aseptic process simulation requirements
* Experience with multiproduct biologics facility start-up is preferred
* Experience interacting with multiple health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA)

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

 
 

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

 
 

**Salary Range (annually)**

$175,700.00 - $292,700.00

new_roles.title: Director, Global Technical Operations – Manufacturing Process and Analytical Science – Analytical
new_roles.description:
**Location** Frederick, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264437 **Date posted** 15/11/2026

 

**Director Biochemical & Biophysical Methods**

**Reports to:** Senior Director, Global Technical Operations – Manufacturing Process and Analytical Science – Analytical

**Location:** Frederick, MD USA

Located on the Frederick, MD Manufacturing Campus, GTO operates a state-of-the-art laboratory equipped with modern analytical instrumentation and small-scale drug substance process capabilities—a truly one-of-a-kind asset within AZ Bio Ops. As Director of Biochemical & Biophysical Methods, you will lead a substantial part of this operation, managing a high-performing team of scientists who serve as subject matter experts (SMEs) for the biochemical and biophysical methods used to release and characterize our late-stage and commercial products. The team's core responsibilities include method validation and transfer, method lifecycle management, manufacturing investigation support, critical reagent qualification, and analytical testing in support of process improvement projects. You will also play a key strategic role in transforming analytical testing within AZ Bio by implementing innovative technologies, leveraging automation to replace manual workflows, and integrating advanced analytical technologies into upstream and downstream manufacturing processes. This is a leadership role where you will partner with peers across internal and external QC testing sites, other GTO functions, R&D, Quality, Regulatory, and Supply Chain organizations to ensure a continuous supply of medicines to patients.

**Typical Accountabilities:**
-----------------------------

* Lead a team that is responsible for execution of all biochemical and biophysical methods including capillary electrophoresis/focusing, HPLC, UPLC, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, differential scanning calorimetry, and various spectroscopic techniques. Execution of this suite of assays typically support method validation, analytical tech transfer, critical reagent qualification, and process improvement projects.

* Plays a key role in identifying and implementing improvement projects within the lab function including integration of automation/liquid handling into workflows, use of generative AI for report generation, data compilation, and review. Works cross-functionally with peers across the organization to help define next generation analytical strategy across the company.

* Maintain GTO’s lab space in a state of GMP compliance.

* Be able to troubleshoot biochemical and biophysical methods.

* **To succeed in this role, you will need to be self-motivated, innovative, have strong technical and communication skills, and a deep understanding of protein chemistry and relevant methods used to release biological products.**

* **Mentors and develops staff of approximately eight direct reports; this is a people manager role.**

**Education, Qualifications, Skills, and Experience**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree technical field such as Pharmacy, Biology, Chemistry.

* Preferred advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a scientific field

* Subject matter expert in multiple biochemical and biophysical methods including HPLC, UPLC, capillary electrophoresis/focusing, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, and differential scanning calorimetry.

* Minimum 10 years of experience working in the pharmaceutical industry.

* Working experience in supervisory / managerial roles within quality in the Pharmaceutical Industry.

* Experience working with regulatory / SOP / GxP requirements and driving compliance.

* Leading complex projects / operations in terms of resources, vendors, and budgets.

* Driving substantial change initiatives through internal/external teams and partners

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $174,856-$262,285 USD However, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition, our positions offer a short-term incentive bonus opportunity; eligibility to participate in our equity-based long-term incentive program. Benefits offered included a qualified retirement program [401(k) plan]; paid vacation and holidays; paid leaves; and, health benefits including medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans. Additional details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment. If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That is why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that does not mean we are not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility.

**Date Posted**

16-Nov-2026

**Closing Date**

25-Feb-2027

Our mission is to build an inclusive environment where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and employees. In furtherance of that mission, we welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their protected characteristics. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please complete the corresponding section in the application form.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**U C Coatings Director of Operations**

**Reports to** President

**Location** Based at a U-C Coatings facility; Buffalo, NY or Kenosha, WI preferred

**Travel** Approximately 25-35%, including regular travel to all four sites and 3PL partners

**Scope** Buffalo, Kenosha, Seattle and Portland manufacturing sites; 3PLs; supply chain and sourcing; customer service

**Position summary**

U-C Coatings manufactures specialty coatings, wood protection and repair products for industrial and consumer markets. The **Director of Operations** leads the people, processes and resources that turn customer demand into safe, reliable production and accurate, timely delivery.

Reporting to the President, this leader is accountable for operating performance across four sites and the supporting supply chain, sourcing, logistics and customer service functions. The role requires regular time on the production floor, strong financial judgment, and the ability to develop capable site and functional leaders in a lean organization.

**Manufacturing and site leadership**

* Lead site leaders in Buffalo, NY, Kenosha, WI, Seattle, WA, and Portland, OR; establish clear responsibilities, operating standards and performance expectations across the network.
* Translate demand into production, staffing and capacity plans; improve batch scheduling, filling, packaging, labor productivity and equipment utilization.
* Improve yield, reduce scrap and rework, and address recurring downtime through preventive maintenance, root cause analysis and practical process improvements.
* Evaluate production allocation, interplant transfers, capital investments and facility changes to improve service, cost and available capacity.

**Supply chain and sourcing**

* Own procurement and supplier performance for raw materials, packaging, purchased products and operating supplies; negotiate pricing, terms and service commitments.
* Lead monthly demand and supply planning with Sales and Finance; align forecasts, purchasing and production with service goals and working capital requirements.
* Set replenishment and inventory policies by item and site; improve inventory accuracy, reduce excess and obsolete stock, and prevent material shortages.
* Develop qualified alternate sources and continuity plans for critical inputs; coordinate supplier and material changes with Technical and Quality before implementation.

**Logistics and third party warehousing**

* Manage 3PL contracts, service standards and performance reviews, including inventory reconciliation, order accuracy, shipping performance, claims and invoice audits.
* Control inbound, outbound, parcel, LTL and interplant freight costs; improve packaging, carrier selection and routing while meeting customer requirements.

**Customer Service**

* Lead Customer Service from order receipt through fulfillment; improve order entry accuracy, acknowledgments, delivery commitments and response times.
* Connect Customer Service, Sales, planning, plants and 3PLs so customers receive reliable commitments and proactive updates on shortages or delays.
* Resolve escalated service issues, returns and credits with Sales, Finance and Technical; use complaint and shipping error trends to eliminate repeat failures.

**Safety quality and compliance**

* Hold site leaders accountable for safe operations, training, inspections, incident reporting and timely corrective action; maintain clear escalation and stop-work authority.
* Partner with internal specialists and outside advisers to meet applicable workplace safety, environmental, storage, waste and shipping requirements at each site.
* Ensure operating teams follow approved formulations, batch records, quality checks, labeling and lot traceability; support product launches and process changes with Technical and Quality.

**Financial management and people leadership**

* Own operating budgets and explain labor, material, freight and overhead variances with Finance; deliver verified savings and capital projects with clear returns.
* Coach and evaluate site and functional leaders; build staffing, cross-training and succession plans, and address performance issues promptly with HR support.
* Run weekly site and consolidated scorecard reviews covering service, cost, quality, inventory and people; assign owners and deadlines and verify corrective actions.

**Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including at least five years leading managers or major operating functions.
* Demonstrated success leading multiple manufacturing sites or a comparably complex manufacturing and distribution network; ability to lead dispersed teams.
* Practical experience with procurement, inventory planning, logistics, outsourced warehousing and customer fulfillment; strong cost and financial analysis skills.
* Experience with ERP and MRP systems, Excel, operating scorecards and continuous improvement; ability to turn data into decisions and sustained results.
* Bachelor's degree in operations, supply chain, engineering, business or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Coatings, chemicals, adhesives, sealants or other batch manufacturing experience is strongly preferred.

**Measures of success**

Accountable measures include safety controls; on-time, in-full delivery; labor efficiency; yield and cost of poor quality; inventory accuracy and turns; supplier and 3PL performance; freight costs; order accuracy; and leadership development. Agree on targets with the CEO after validating baselines.

**Initial priorities and working environment**

Within 90 days, assess the sites and key partners, validate scorecards, and agree on an improvement plan with owners, deadlines and financial impact. Work includes office, plant and warehouse activities, required PPE (company-provided), regular travel and occasional support outside business hours. Essential duties may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

**COMPANY DESCRIPTION:**

U-C Coatings is a leading manufacturer and supplier of premium wood protection products. For more than 50 years, our products have been used in a variety of industries, including hardwood and softwood logging and lumber production, wood products, manufacturing, woodworking, and wood decking markets.

Our products are used worldwide to protect, conserve, and enhance forest resources. Our goal is to help our customers achieve more with less waste and provide the highest level of protection for their products.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:**

This role is an in-person role located within the company’s Kenosha, WI location. There is a moderate noise level within the work environment. Compliance with applicable Company policies including maintaining a drug-free workplace and adhering to all safety policies and procedures is required.

**DISCLAIMERS:**

UC Coatings, LLC reserves the right to revise, change or modify the duties and responsibilities of this position at any time to meet business needs. This job description may not list all duties for this position. This job description is not a contract of employment, and all UC Coatings, LLC employment unless otherwise disclosed is “at will” and either the incumbent or UC Coatings, LLC may terminate employment at any time for any reason.

UC Coatings, LLC is an Equal opportunity, inclusive employer and will consider all applicants for employment with the Company based on merit, competence, and qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Operations management: 5 years (Required)

Willingness to travel:

* 50% (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Contract Manufacturing Director
new_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $165,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The **Director, Contract Manufacturing** reports to the Vice President, Integrated Planning, U.S. Beverage and is based in Cherry Hill, New Jersey.

The Director is responsible for defining the role of contract manufacturing within the Beverage Division’s broader supply network and translating business plans into clear external capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership requirements across the U.S. and Canada. This role leads the development and optimization of the contract manufacturing network to ensure the right capabilities, capacity, cost, quality, service, and resilience to support business growth.

The Director oversees relationships with contract manufacturing partners from initial capability assessment and commercial selection through operational integration, product launch, ongoing governance, and continuous performance improvement.

The Director aligns internal business and functional leaders around external manufacturing decisions and builds productive relationships with strategic partners. The role ensures that external manufacturing resources are positioned to support the division’s growth plans, innovation agenda, service expectations, cost objectives, and business continuity requirements.

**Up to 25% travel required**

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**External Manufacturing Strategy & Network Optimization**

* Define and execute the contract manufacturing strategy for the Beverage Division across the U.S. and Canada, translating business requirements into external manufacturing capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership needs.
* Optimize the existing contract manufacturing network by assessing manufacturing capabilities, capacity, geographic footprint, technology, cost, service, quality, and supply risk.
* Partner with Integrated Planning, Operations, Finance, Procurement, and other key stakeholders on make-versus-buy decisions and long-term capacity strategies.
* Maintain a strong understanding of the external manufacturing landscape to identify new capabilities, technologies, potential partners, and opportunities to strengthen the overall supply network.

**Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management**

* Translate business requirements into sourcing strategies for externally manufactured products, balancing economics, available capacity, technical capability, speed, flexibility, and supply risk.
* Lead competitive sourcing and partner-selection activities, including market assessment, RFIs/RFPs/RFQs, commercial evaluation, supplier selection, negotiation, contracting, and implementation.
* Structure and negotiate commercial agreements that clearly define pricing, capacity commitments, service expectations, quality requirements, flexibility provisions, liability, and business continuity obligations.
* Develop fact-based sourcing recommendations considering total cost of ownership, capacity, capability, risk, and overall strategic fit.
* Establish pricing mechanisms and commercial frameworks that promote transparency, competitiveness, and sustainable productivity.
* Provide financial stewardship of external manufacturing spend through disciplined budgeting, forecasting, cost analysis, variance management, and productivity delivery.

**Supplier Relationship & Performance Management**

* Establish and lead a structured Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) approach for strategic contract manufacturing partners.
* Establish and maintain a robust performance management framework and supplier scorecards for the contract manufacturing network.
* Establish a disciplined operating rhythm with strategic partners, supported by agreed performance measures, periodic operating and executive business reviews, documented recovery plans, and clear ownership of actions.
* Build strategic relationships with key external manufacturing partners to improve service, strengthen capacity and flexibility, accelerate innovation, and identify productivity opportunities.
* Lead supplier and network risk assessments and ensure appropriate business continuity, contingency, and risk mitigation plans are developed and maintained.

The Director owns the performance framework for the external manufacturing network, ensuring that targets reflect the division’s priorities for customer service, product quality, delivered cost, productivity, available capacity, launch execution, contractual compliance, and supply continuity. The role is responsible for converting performance information into timely decisions, recovery actions, and clear visibility of results and risks for business leadership.

**Commercialization & Cross-Functional Execution**

* Lead the external manufacturing workstream for new product commercialization, capacity expansions, product transfers, and new contract manufacturer onboarding.
* Partner with R&D, Marketing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Integrated Planning, and other key functions to ensure new products and external manufacturing capabilities are launched on time, at target cost, and in accordance with quality and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure effective integration of contract manufacturers into the broader planning and supply network, including capacity planning, production planning, inventory management, service, and supply continuity.
* Coordinate resolution of operational and supply issues across internal functions and external manufacturing partners, ensuring clear ownership and escalating material business risks when required.

**Team Leadership & Governance**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Contract Manufacturing team, establishing clear goals, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Establish the governance, processes, tools, decision rights, and performance standards required to effectively manage the external manufacturing network.
* Ensure accurate and actionable contract manufacturing information is maintained, including supplier capabilities, capacity, pricing, commercial terms, products/SKUs, performance, and contractual commitments.
* Provide business leadership with regular visibility into external manufacturing cost, capacity, service, performance, supply risk, and opportunities, enabling timely and informed decision-making.
* Drive cross-functional alignment and accountability for initiatives and decisions affecting the external manufacturing network.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in contract manufacturing, external manufacturing, strategic sourcing, procurement, operations, or supply chain, preferably within the CPG, food, or beverage industry.
* Demonstrated experience managing third-party manufacturing relationships and complex commercial agreements.
* Strong experience in strategic sourcing, supplier negotiations, contracting, and supplier relationship management.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving Operations, Planning, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial teams.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate cost, capacity, capability, service, quality, and supply risk and translate analysis into effective business recommendations.
* Strong financial and analytical acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, cost modeling, and productivity initiatives.
* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and external business partners within a complex matrix organization.
* Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, problem-solving, and change-management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food, beverage, or broader CPG industry.
* Experience managing a multi-site or North American external manufacturing network.
* Experience with new product commercialization, manufacturing transfers, and external partner onboarding.
* APICS/ASCM certification, CPSM, or comparable supply chain/procurement certification.
* MBA or advanced degree.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Directly manages three employees, providing coaching, development, performance management, and clear accountability for results.
* Establishes team priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with the contract manufacturing strategy and broader business goals.
* Builds team capability and expertise while fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement, and results.
* Provides leadership across a broader cross-functional network, influencing internal stakeholders and external manufacturing partners to achieve service, quality, cost, capacity, innovation, and supply continuity objectives.
* Leads through influence across a matrix organization, driving alignment and accountability among internal functions and strategic external partners.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle, taking the plane, doing north American travel and occasionally working in the field.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

**OCCASIONAL:** squatting, kneeling, reach above and at shoulder height, moderate grasp to manipulate reference books and manuals; lifting objects weighing 20 – 35 lbs. from below waist to above shoulders and transporting distances up to 50 feet.

**VISION:** Ability to see in the normal visual range with or without correction.

**HEARING:** Ability to hear in the normal audio range with or without correction.

Other duties as assigned are part of every job description. The conditions herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform essential job functions.**

new_roles.title: Digital Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
Some people manage teams. Others build environments where elite technical talent thrives, innovation accelerates, and customers become lifelong advocates. We’re looking for a Digital Plant Manager who can do all three.

This isn’t a “keep the trains running” management role. We need a leader who can build and steward high-performing Agile teams, drive operational excellence, own financial outcomes, and help shape the future of Vertech’s Digital Plant organization. You’ll lead self-organizing Scrum teams delivering world class industrial automation and software solutions while guiding strategic investments in internal development tools and accelerators that improve how we work and scale.

If you know how to balance leadership with accountability, coaching with execution, and strategy with action—and you genuinely enjoy helping talented people do the best work of their careers—we should probably talk.

**Who We Are**

At Vertech, not only do we develop world class industrial automation solutions for some of the top US companies, we also strive to be the team of choice for the best and brightest talent. I mean, we call ourselves control freaks for a reason.

The passion (and intelligence) our employees have is truly mind-blowing. In turn, we work hard to take care of our own with excellent benefits and pay, personal development, and transparent communication. We also know that you can be great at what you do and still have fun.

If that sounds like a good fit, help us bring the next generation of automation solutions to industries including data centers, renewable energy, manufacturing, food and beverage, water and wastewater, and more.

**Top Reasons to Work with Us**

* Flexible work schedule with work from home options for many roles
* Weekly communication from management in our internally famous Friday morning meeting
* Competitive compensation including a bonus plan
* No more than a 4 week waiting period on all benefits including the 401k
* A really rad Christmas Party each year
* A manager that is cool…most of the time, because no one is perfect
* A path for growth, a great culture, PTO, AND MORE!

**What You Will Be Doing**

* Build, lead, and develop high-performing Professional Scrum teams capable of delivering world class customer outcomes
* Coach, mentor, and support team members through consistent feedback, career development, and leadership
* Ensure teams are staffed with the right people in the right roles while fostering Vertech’s culture and core values
* Own the financial performance and delivery outcomes of projects executed by your teams
* Serve as the primary escalation point for customers beyond the execution team
* Drive operational excellence using Professional Agile Leadership (PAL-E), Scrum principles, and Evidence Based Management (EBM)
* Govern and prioritize Digital Plant’s portfolio of internal software accelerators and development tools
* Partner with leadership to contribute to strategic planning and organizational growth initiatives
* Ensure investment initiatives are properly staffed, organized, funded, and aligned with company objectives
* Promote continuous improvement in delivery execution, technical excellence, and team collaboration
* Work closely with HR and leadership on hiring, onboarding, employee growth, and team performance
* Help create an environment where highly technical people genuinely enjoy coming to work

**What You Need for this Position**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field (or equivalent industry experience)
* Deep expertise in Agile frameworks, Professional Scrum, and Professional Agile Leadership (PAL-E)
* 7+ years of experience in industrial automation and systems integration
* 3+ years of leadership experience with accountability for team success
* Strong understanding of software and industrial systems development methodologies including Agile, DevOps, CI/CD, and related practices
* Proven ability to lead technical teams while balancing customer satisfaction, delivery quality, and financial performance
* Excellent communication, organizational, and leadership skills
* Strong business acumen including understanding of project financials, margins, utilization, and operational efficiency

**Bonus Points If You Have**

* Experience leading multiple Scrum teams simultaneously
* Background in software product or platform development
* Experience scaling Agile delivery organizations
* Passion for coaching and developing technical talent
* A desire to build systems and teams that continuously improve over time

**Why This Role Matters**

The Digital Plant Manager plays a critical role in Vertech’s vision to be recognized as a world class provider of industrial automation services—and the employer of choice for top talent. This role directly influences our people, our customers, our delivery capabilities, and the future of how we scale Digital Plant operations.

No pressure. But also…kind of a big deal.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
Our Plant Manager is responsible for the daily production processing of our Laundry facility. Managing the employees in our production, warehouse, and maintenance departments, you will be responsible for monitoring production flow, controlling costs, maintaining quality standards, and regulating product inventory. Managerial duties include all staffing, transfer, promotion, coaching, training, terminating, and employee review responsibilities.

**Requirements:**

* We require 1+ years of managerial or supervisory experience, in a production environment
* Qualified candidates should have previous experience controlling budgets, setting schedules, and meeting production deadlines
* Production-line scheduling experience
* Staff scheduling experience
* Lean management experience utilizing computer controls
* Must be growth oriented and career minded
* Good communication skills are required
* Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred but not required
* Bachelors Degree Preferred.

**Benefits of working at Prudential Overall Supply:**

* Competitive hourly rate. We know your time and hard work is valuable!
* Exceptional Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* Paid Time Off for vacation, holidays and sick time
* Full Tuition Reimbursement
* Paid Life Insurance
* 401K with company match
* Profit sharing. When we do well as a company, you do well!
* Regular work schedule, Monday – Friday
* Uniform Provided
* Employee Discounts
* Career development and advancement within the company. Let us help you reach your goals!

**Company History:** Since 1932, Prudential Overall Supply continues to provide best-in-class solutions for a business’ uniform and textile needs. Service programs include uniform rental, uniform lease, uniform purchase for industrial uniform programs and related services. We have been deemed essential in the services we provide to our clients and community. Prudential is grateful for the exceptional work produced by our industry-best tenured employees, and to our exceptional customer patronage. It is this connection that enables Prudential to provide our customers with the best possible products and service at a fair price, today and into the future.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** Prudential Overall Supply is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or employing any individual on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ancestry, religion, physical or intellectual disability, age veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, pregnancy, citizenship, or any other factor protected by anti-discriminatory laws

new_roles.title: Plant Manager - West Chicago
new_roles.description:
Company Statement: Graham Packaging is a people, planet and values-based company and a leader in sustainable packaging manufacturing. From the kitchen to the laundry room, Graham Packaging is part of your everyday life. For employees at Graham, our Blue Culture is part of their everyday lives, too. In other words, Blue is how we do things here. At Graham, we are united by a clear vision. We know our part and help those around us know theirs, encouraging one another to continuously improve. We create a safe, challenging environment to innovate by supporting creative ideas and new ways of thinking. We take the initiative to cultivate our individual growth and help others do the same, while keeping ourselves and one another accountable. And we actively promote cooperation, collaboration, integrity and respect across regions and teams to foster an engaged, diverse and connected workforce. We value our employees, and a Blue Culture allows for the most rewarding employee experience as part of the Graham family. Blue is how we feel about what we do—together—to create a better tomorrow. Working at Graham means you lead constructively with clear goals, use diverse thinking to drive excellence, accountability, innovation, as well as demonstrating collaboration, embracing learning, and taking action for continuous improvement and growth. Overview:

Plant Managers are responsible for overall effectiveness of day-to-day manufacturing operations through direction of personnel in the management of safety, quality, customer service, efficient utilization of resources, equipment, materials and manpower procedures and programs. The primary duties of a Plant Manager include:

* Understands, follows and enforces all established safety, health, quality GMP and Company policies, procedures and recognized practices.
* Understands, follows and enforces all established policies, procedures and recognized practices.
* Leads the plant safety initiatives through the participation and development of safety training programs, plant safety meetings, safety audits and by encouraging employee involvement through safety suggestion and recognition programs.
* Leads the plant quality initiatives through the implementation of corrective actions from customer or internal complaints, coordinating new product qualifications, and participating in internal and external quality system audits and developing and implementing corrective action plans.
* Responsible for the selection, training, growth and development of shift and staff personnel to attain organizational goals
* Reviews operating statements for all departments and directs manufacturing operations so that all plant costs are within budgetary standards.
* Develops and maintains sound relations with customers and works with them to identify systems improvements and possible supply chain cost reductions.

* Participates in monthly, quarterly and year-end physical inventories in accordance with corporate guidelines.
* Oversee the creation and implementation of plants strategic and tactical plans that provided the needed focus and drive to achieve the plant and overall company objectives.
* Drive continuous improvement plans using Operation Excellence tools across cross functional departments.
* Promote an open door and team building environment policy.
* May be responsible for special projects related to other functional areas

* Ability to maintain regular, predictable, and punctual attendance.
* Computer usage and typing skills are essential.
* Excellent verbal and written communication, including the ability to effectively communicate with internal and external customers.

* Communicates effectively: conveys facts and information clearly both verbally and orally.
* Collaborates well with others: proactively contributes to group objectives; volunteers to help others.

new_roles.title: Market Director, Facility Operations
new_roles.description:
**Join a team that shares your calling**

At MultiCare, you’re more than just a job title — you’re part of a team built on trust that cares for each other, our patients and our communities. Belonging here means living our mission and values every day. If your purpose and passions align with ours, you’ll find a place to grow, do meaningful work and build a career you love in a community that feels like home.

**FTE:** 1.0, **Shift:** Day, **Schedule:** Business hours

**Position Summary**

The Market Director, Facility Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for facility operations across the East Pierce Market within MultiCare Health System, including hospitals, ambulatory sites, urgent care centers, clinics, medical office buildings, and other healthcare facilities. 
 
This role is accountable for market-level facility operations, plant operations, building systems, property management, regulatory compliance, infrastructure reliability, and facility-related operational planning.
 
 
The Market Director serves as the primary operational partner between East Pierce Market leadership and system Facilities Management & Operations Support Services (FMOSS), Planning, Design & Construction, Real Estate, and other enterprise support teams. 
 
The position supports the growth and development of acute care, ambulatory, and ambulatory surgery center (ASC) services throughout the market by ensuring facility readiness, property management, operational integration, infrastructure performance, and strategic alignment with organizational objectives.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute market-based facility operations strategies that support MultiCare Health System goals, market growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and exceptional patient and caregiver experiences.
* Provide operational leadership for facility operations across East Pierce Market hospitals, ambulatory care centers, urgent care locations, clinics, medical office buildings, and future expansion sites.
* Administer and maintain departmental services in accordance with standards established by The Joint Commission, CMS, Washington State Department of Health, NFPA, OSHA, and other applicable regulatory agencies to ensure compliance and operational readiness.
* Oversee the operation, maintenance, reliability, and performance of facility infrastructure systems including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, medical gas, utility distribution, fire and life safety systems, and vertical transportation.
* Partner with system Planning, Design, Construction, Real Estate, FMOSS, and executive leadership teams to support enterprise capital initiatives, facility modernization programs, infrastructure investments, and market growth priorities.
* Provide local operational leadership and accountability for facility improvement projects, renovations, repairs, and capital projects within delegated market authority.
* Support the development and expansion of ambulatory care services and Ambulatory Surgery Centers (ASCs) through facility planning, operational readiness activities, site assessments, and coordination with system stakeholders.
* Contribute to long-range facility, infrastructure, and space planning efforts that support the East Pierce Market's strategic growth objectives.
* Oversee market property management activities, including leased and owned properties, landlord relationships, facility condition management, operational readiness, occupancy coordination, and vendor performance.
* Partner with Organizational Compliance, Environment of Care, Emergency Management, and Safety leaders to ensure effective implementation of Environment of Care, Life Safety, Emergency Preparedness, and related regulatory programs throughout the market.
* Manage resource allocation, operational budgets, workforce planning, contracted services, and performance metrics to optimize organizational effectiveness and asset stewardship.
* Facilitate coordination between hospital leadership, ambulatory leadership, physicians, FMOSS, and operational teams to ensure facility services support clinical and business objectives.
* Oversee minor construction, infrastructure upgrades, and facility enhancement projects while ensuring minimal disruption to patient care and business operations.
* Participate in market strategic planning initiatives and provide facility expertise to support operational growth, service line expansion, and future care delivery models.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, Engineering, Construction Management, Facilities Management, Public Administration, or related field required.
* Master's Degree preferred.
* Eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare facility operations, plant operations, property management, capital project coordination, regulatory compliance, engineering, or related operational leadership functions.
* Five (5) years of experience with The Joint Commission standards, including Environment of Care, Life Safety, Emergency Management, and regulatory compliance requirements.
* Five (5) years of management or supervisory experience with direct budget, operational, and personnel responsibilities.
* Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with planning, design, construction, real estate, property management, and executive leadership teams on healthcare facility initiatives.
* Experience supporting hospital and ambulatory healthcare operations in a multi-site healthcare environment preferred.
* Knowledge of healthcare facility infrastructure systems, regulatory requirements, facility operations, capital planning processes, and property management principles.

**About Good Samaritan Hospital**

MultiCare Good Samaritan Hospital is a 388-bed acute-care hub serving Puyallup and East Pierce County. As the area’s only hospital, it features a Family Birth Center, Level III Trauma and Neonatal ICUs, Level I Trauma Rehabilitation Center, Children’s Therapy Unit and a 24-hour Emergency Department. Innovative facilities like the LEED Gold-certified Dally Tower and Pulse Heart Institute make Good Samaritan a dynamic workplace for clinicians eager to advance their careers in a state-of-the-art environment.

**About the Puyallup Community**

Nestled at the foot of Mount Rainier along the Puyallup River, Puyallup offers a welcoming small-town feel just 10 miles from Tacoma and 35 miles from Seattle. Residents enjoy unique dining, an antique-filled downtown, excellent schools and abundant parks and recreation — all while being close to big-city opportunities.

**Why MultiCare?**

**Rooted in the local community**

Partnering with patients, families and neighbors across the Pacific Northwest for more than 140 years.

**Growth and education**

Competitive tuition assistance, award-winning residencies, fellowships and career development to invest in you.

**Well-being and support**

Generous PTO, Code Lavender and Employee Assistance Programs to help you maintain balance and feel cared in your work and life.

**Living our values**

Respect, integrity, kindness and collaboration guide how we care for patients, communities and each other.

**Belonging for all**

Resource Groups and outreach programs help ensure every team member feels safe, seen, heard and valued.

**Pacific Northwest lifestyle**

Work and live where natural beauty, adventure and strong community connections are part of everyday life.

**Pay and Benefit Expectations**

We provide a comprehensive benefits package, including competitive salary, medical, dental and retirement benefits and paid time off. As required by various pay transparency laws, we share a competitive range of compensation for candidates hired into each position. The pay scale is $163,113.60 - $234,707.20 USD. However, pay is influenced by factors specific to applicants, including but not limited to: skill set, level of experience, and certification(s) and/or education. If this position is associated with a union contract, pay will be reflective of the appropriate step on the pay scale to which the applicant’s years of experience align.

Associated benefit information can be viewed here.

new_roles.title: Chemical Manufacturing Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Company Summary:**

We are a fast-growing, innovative company that is revolutionizing global health. At Vireo and pH-D you will be on the ground-floor of an exciting fast-growing company that focuses on its core values and is passionate about improving the lives of people and pets by delivering premium, health products through world-class research innovation and manufacturing.

**Position Summary:**

The Plant Manager has full operational accountability for the chemical manufacturing facility at Vireo Resources in Plattsmouth, Nebraska. This leader owns facility performance from raw material readiness through batch execution, finished product handoff, and shipment readiness. The role delivers safe, consistent, efficient, and cost-effective batches that meet approved specifications and production commitments, with direct accountability for people, production, manufacturing cost, equipment reliability, and continuous improvement.

**Role and Responsibilities:**

* **Operational Leadership:** Lead facility operations across all shifts, aligning production schedules, staffing, materials, and equipment availability to meet demand. Manage budgets and drive improvements in productivity, cost, quality, and delivery.
* **Process and Technical Leadership:** Apply chemistry and engineering expertise to improve manufacturing processes and resolve recurring issues. Partner with cross-functional teams to lead startups, establish operating standards, and ensure consistent execution of approved procedures.
* **Safety, Quality, and Compliance:** Ensure operations meet safety, environmental, and quality requirements. Oversee chemical handling, process safety, and emergency readiness, and lead corrective actions with EHS and Quality while preserving Quality’s independent product release authority.
* **People Leadership:** Hire, coach, and develop facility teams, ensuring effective shift coverage and employee competency. Establish clear expectations and reinforce accountability, collaboration, and Vireo’s core values.
* **Strategic Planning and Performance:** Develop capacity and improvement plans that support company growth. Execute approved capital projects and communicate operational results, financial performance, risks, and recovery plans to leadership.

**Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree or above in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related field.
* 8+ years in chemical manufacturing, including 3+ years leading plant operations. Experience must include people, production, and budget accountability.
* Proven batch manufacturing leadership with measurable improvements in yield, cycle time, quality, output, and cost.
* Strong budgeting, cost analysis, capacity planning, and KPI management skills.
* Strong knowledge of chemical processes, reaction engineering, utilities, and automated controls. Translate technical issues into practical decisions and communicate clearly.
* Ability to lead a 24/7 operation and respond to urgent operating issues.
* Proven ability to develop teams, set expectations, and hold employees accountable.
* Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis skills. Demonstrated success preventing recurring failures.
* Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, or similar improvement methods. Certification preferred.
* Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, quality, and compliance. Plant startup, commissioning, or expansion experience preferred.
* Travel up to 10%

**Physical Demands / Work Environment:**

* Ability to stand, walk, climb stairs, and perform essential plant duties, with or without reasonable accommodation up to 10 hours.
* Must be able to occasionally lift up to 50 pounds
* Ability to work around chemicals, heat, noise, and equipment using required safeguards and PPE.
* Availability for extended hours or weekends during startup, outages, emergencies, and critical operations.

**Compensation + Benefits:**

* Base salary + bonus based on company and personal performance
* Medical, Dental, Vision and Supplement Insurance (with company assistance)
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid Time off, 9.5 Paid Holidays

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Company Description**

Sirtex Medical is a global leader in healthcare, with offices in the U.S., Australia, Germany, and Singapore, dedicated to improving patient outcomes.

Our mission is to be at the forefront of minimally invasive cancer and embolization therapies. By partnering with physicians, we aim to provide innovative products that enhance patient outcomes and simplify treatments. Achieving this ambitious goal requires passionate and talented individuals who are committed to making a difference. Our flagship product, SIR-Spheres® Y-90 resin microspheres, is a targeted radiation therapy for liver cancer. To date, we have delivered over >150K doses across 50+ countries, significantly impacting patients' lives worldwide. Our success is fueled by our dedication to serving the medical community, maintaining professionalism, fostering a collaborative work culture, nurturing an entrepreneurial spirit, and continuously pursuing innovation and improvement.

At Sirtex, we are committed to creating a great workplace. We offer a range of benefits, programs, and services to support our employees, ensuring they have opportunities to contribute to our success and advance their careers. Join our inclusive community, where you can collaborate with talented colleagues, bring your ideas to life, and advance your career, all while delivering innovative healthcare solutions to patients.

 **Job Description**

**SCOPE:**

The Wilmington plant is the largest of 3 global Sirtex manufacturing site and serves as the principal production site of both SIR-Spheres microspheres and Lava product lines. The Plant Manager is responsible for leading the sites manufacturing operations, engineering, warehouse and product distribution.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

 

* Develop and lead execution of the site manufacturing strategy for both the SIR-Spheres and Lava value streams. Align site goals with Senior Leadership and Corporate objectives.
* Team Performance Management: lead, develop and mentor manufacturing team members.
* Manage production schedules, ensuring resource availability and capacity to meet demand, working closely with the Supply Chain team, using optimal schedules to minimize overall costs.
* Lead Continuous Improvement efforts, identifying process, equipment, product, and other opportunities, that reduce cost, improve quality and safety at the site.
* Full responsibility for developing and managing to site budget.
* Ensure resource and equipment capacity to ensure efficient and reliable manufacturing.
* Set site target KPI’s managing OEE, Labor Efficiency, Scrap, Equipment Utilization, etc.
* Ensure product is built to specification and in compliance with all Quality System requirements.
* Manage the site engineering team to ensure equipment and processes are robust and meet all manufacturing requirements. Manage PM strategy and ensure that execution is completed on time.
* Support the Quality Department, working with on site Quality team members to ensure that compliance with all areas of the Sirtex QMS are being followed. Identify opportunities for improvement and work to implement them directly in the QMS.
* Work in conjunction with HSE/Facilities Department to ensure a safe working environment for all employees and that the facilities is maintained, and compliant with regulatory requirements for both the handling of radioactive materials and medical device manufacturing.
* Manage all shipping, receiving and warehousing activities. Ensure timely material receipt, inventory accuracy is maintained, and products are shipped on time.

 
**Qualifications**

**EDUCATIONAL PREREQUISITES AND SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or related discipline such as Chemistry or Biomedical field
* 5+ Years experience working in medical device or pharmaceutical industry preferred.
* Prior experience working with radioisotopes preferred.
* 3+ years of site management experience, with 10+ years of leadership experience.
* 6 Sigma Green belt preferred. Experience using 5S and Lean principles is preferred.

The anticipated annual base salary range and target bonus opportunity is $136,000 to $171,000 annually, plus a 15% target annual bonus.

The final position level and compensation will be determined based on non-discriminatory, job-related factors, including geographic location, skills, experience, education, and alignment with the position requirements. In addition to base salary and bonus eligibility, Sirtex offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid sick and vacation time, medical, dental, vision and life insurance, and a generous 401(k) matching program and other benefits, subject to applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements.

 **Additional Information**

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines

Do you want to be part of something bigger? A team whose impact stretches across the globe making a real difference to the quality of people’s lives. Sirtex recognizes that well-being, financial health, and work-life balance are crucial for our employees to achieve personal success.

Sirtex offers qualified candidates:

* Diverse and flexible work arrangements to achieve the optimum balance between work and personal responsibilities.
* A culture of respect, diversity, collaboration, and innovation fostering inclusiveness and superior performance.
* Attractive compensation and benefit packages which are practical, robust and equitable.
* A commitment to support ongoing professional growth through career development, on the job experiences and training opportunities.
* Challenging work which supports the development of new and better ways to improve clinical outcomes for oncology treatment around the world.
* An unwavering commitment to company values, employee safety and excellence in everything we do.

Diversity drives innovation; inclusion fosters belonging, growth and success. Sirtex believes that it takes multiple perspectives and voices to create a culture and workplace which fosters engagement, teamwork, and employee satisfaction to perform our best and deliver on commitments. We are dedicated to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, included, and can share their ideas so that we can exceed even our own expectations.

Sirtex is An Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status, age or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Sirtex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.
