With a legacy spanning over 35 years, Harris Spice has been a trusted partner and leading supplier of high-quality spices, herbs, and innovative seasoning blends. With international facilities and a global supply chain, we proudly serve multiple channels of trade—including industrial bulk, food service, and retail. Our commitment to excellence, quality and consistency has earned us the trust of some of the nation’s largest and most recognized brands. As Harris Spice continues to grow, we are dedicated to cultivating a dynamic, inclusive workplace where innovation thrives. We're looking for diverse, talented individuals who are ready to grow with us and help strengthen a brand known for trust, quality, and bold flavor solutions.

**Position Overview/Job Summary:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership and performance of the manufacturing facility, overseeing Production and Maintenance, and Planning & Scheduling as assigned. This role ensures safe, efficient, and cost-effective operations while meeting production targets, customer demand, quality standards, and food safety requirements. The Plant Manager drives operational excellence, equipment reliability, continuous improvement, and cost control while developing a strong, accountable team to achieve the company's business objectives.

**Essential Job Functions:**

· Provide overall leadership and direction for plant operations to achieve production, quality, safety, service, and financial objectives.

· Oversee Production and Maintenance, and Planning & Scheduling as assigned.

· Establish departmental goals, KPIs, and performance expectations aligned with company objectives.

· Ensure adequate staffing, equipment, materials, and resources to meet operational demands.

· Monitor plant performance, address operational challenges, and drive improvements in productivity, efficiency, and capacity.

· Ensure effective coordination between departments and hold managers and supervisors accountable for results.

· Oversee production activities to ensure products are manufactured safely, on schedule, within quality standards, and at standard cost.

· Monitor production performance, labor efficiency, material usage, waste, downtime, and OEE.

· Analyze production reports and KPIs to identify performance gaps and implement corrective actions.

· Drive continuous improvement initiatives to increase productivity, improve yields, reduce waste, and optimize manufacturing processes.

· Ensure compliance with established SOPs and operational standards.

· Oversee Maintenance to ensure equipment, facilities, and infrastructure are properly maintained and operational.

· Establish and monitor preventive and predictive maintenance programs to minimize downtime and improve equipment reliability.

· Coordinate maintenance activities with production schedules to minimize operational disruptions.

· Monitor maintenance expenses, repair costs, and equipment performance.

· Implement equipment improvements, capital projects, and cost reduction initiatives.

· Oversee production planning and scheduling to align customer demand with production capacity, labor availability, and raw material inventory.

· Ensure production schedules are achievable and effectively communicated across departments.

· Coordinate with Supply Chain, Purchasing, and Customer Service to ensure material availability and minimize scheduling disruptions.

· Monitor schedule attainment and implement improvements to production flow and planning efficiency.

· Manage plant operating expenses and departmental budgets to achieve established financial targets.

· Identify opportunities to reduce manufacturing costs, improve labor utilization, and minimize material waste.

· Monitor plant KPIs, including production output, labor efficiency, OEE, downtime, waste, quality, and maintenance costs.

· Review departmental scorecards and performance reports to identify trends, address variances, and drive operational improvements.

· Ensure facility compliance with food safety regulations, GMPs, HACCP requirements, and company quality standards.

· Partner with Quality Assurance to maintain food safety programs and ensure consistent product quality.

· Ensure employees follow established SOPs, allergen controls, and food safety procedures.

· Support internal and external audits and ensure timely resolution of findings and corrective actions.

· Promote a culture of food safety and quality throughout the facility.

· Promote a proactive safety culture through hazard identification, employee training, incident prevention, and accountability.

· Lead, develop, and coach department managers and supervisors to achieve operational goals.

· Partner with Human Resources on staffing, recruitment, employee development, and succession planning.

· Foster a culture of accountability, teamwork, communication, and continuous improvement throughout the facility.

· Other duties as assigned.

· This job description describes some of the main duties, activities, and responsibilities for the role, which may change at any time with or without prior notice.

**Skills/Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Operations Management, Food Science, or related field preferred.
* 10+ years of manufacturing management experience, preferably in food manufacturing or high-speed automated operations.
* Minimum 7 years of experience managing multiple departments, managers, and/or supervisors.
* Strong knowledge of production operations, maintenance systems, equipment reliability, and plant management.
* Proven ability to improve productivity, reduce costs, manage budgets, and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience with manufacturing KPIs, including OEE, labor efficiency, downtime, waste, and production yield.
* Strong understanding of food safety systems, including GMP, HACCP, BRC, or SQF, and OSHA requirements.
* Proficient in Microsoft Office and ERP/MRP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to lead teams, manage competing priorities, and drive accountability and results.
* Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.

**Physical Requirements**

· Ability to stand and walk throughout the facility for extended periods, including 8–10-hour shifts as operationally required.

· Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and climb ladders when necessary.

· Ability to work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to heat, noise, and food processing equipment.

existing_roles.description:
**Director, New Product Introduction (NPI) & Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)**

Round Rock, Texas | Onsite | Full-Time

**Reports to:** CFO/CEO

**Works closely with:** Director of Operations/Engineering/R&D, Quality, Purchasing, Production, Program Management and external suppliers

**Travel:** Approximately 25%-35%, primarily to supplier locations

**Role structure:** Hands-on director role; initially an individual contributor leading cross-functional work

**Role Summary**

The Director of NPI & PLM leads the transition of new and modified products from development into stable production. The role coordinates product documentation, supplier readiness, pilot builds, production handoff and lifecycle changes across Ametrine and its manufacturing partners.

This position is focused on practical execution. The Director will work directly with cut-and-sew partners and other suppliers to ensure products can be produced repeatedly at the required quality, capacity and schedule. The role also helps develop alternate sources and contingency plans across fabric, metallization, printing, DWR treatment and cut-and-sew operations.

**Primary Responsibilities**

**New Product Introduction**

* Maintain the NPI schedule for new products, product changes and manufacturing transfers.
* Coordinate requirements, design release, sourcing, prototype builds, pilot production, validation and production handoff.
* Use clear stage gates, owners, due dates and readiness checklists.
* Identify schedule, supplier, material, quality and capacity risks early and drive actions to closure.
* Provide concise status updates covering progress, open decisions, risks and next steps.

**Prototype-to-Production Transfer**

* Work with Engineering and R&D to review designs for manufacturability and production readiness.
* Prepare or coordinate BOMs, routings, work instructions, technical packages, inspection points and packaging requirements.
* Lead prototype, pilot and first-production builds at Ametrine and supplier locations.
* Capture lessons learned and ensure changes are reflected in released documentation.
* Confirm that Operations and suppliers are ready before a product is released to routine production.

**Cut-and-Sew and Supplier Readiness**

* Work onsite with cut-and-sew partners to establish and improve production methods.
* Review patterns, sewing specifications, fixtures, templates, work instructions and inspection requirements.
* Assess supplier labor, equipment, training, floor space, quality controls and available capacity.
* Develop practical ramp plans and verify production rates through actual builds.
* Support supplier training and resolve manufacturability, throughput and quality issues during launch.
* Track supplier actions and escalate missed commitments or unsupported plans.

**Product Lifecycle Management**

* Maintain control of released BOMs, specifications, approved materials, suppliers, routings and product revisions.
* Coordinate engineering changes and assess their impact on inventory, suppliers, schedule, testing and customer requirements.
* Ensure the correct product configuration is used for each order and customer.
* Support PLM process and system improvements, including appropriate integration with ERP/MRP.
* Maintain orderly lifecycle records from product introduction through sustainment and retirement.

**Supply-Chain Resilience**

* Maintain a process-level supply-chain map covering fabric, metallization, printing, DWR, cut and sew, accessories and final delivery.
* Identify bottlenecks, long-lead items, single-source dependencies and supplier-capacity risks.
* Develop and qualify alternate sources where practical.
* Create contingency plans for specialized processes that cannot be economically dual-sourced.
* Coordinate source qualification with Operations, Purchasing, Engineering and Quality.
  

**Quality and Process Control**

* Partner with Quality to define process controls, inspection requirements and first-article expectations.
* Support supplier qualification, process reviews, root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Monitor first-pass yield, defects, rework and launch-related issues.
* Ensure production methods remain consistent with approved documentation and customer requirements.

**Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Lead NPI work through influence across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Purchasing and suppliers.
* Maintain clear owners, deadlines and escalation paths.
* Coordinate with the Director of Operations so new-product timelines and supplier readiness are aligned with the production plan.
* Support communication and coordination between Ametrine Inc. and Ametrine Ltd. where product development activities overlap.

**Success Measures**

* NPI milestones completed on schedule
* Prototype-to-pilot and pilot-to-production cycle time
* Supplier readiness and capacity verification completed before launch
* Percentage of critical supply-chain nodes with an alternate source or documented contingency
* Launch first-pass yield, rework and defect performance
* Completeness and accuracy of BOMs, routings, work instructions and product revisions
* Timely closure of supplier, manufacturing-readiness and lifecycle risks

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, industrial technology, textiles, supply chain or a related field; equivalent directly relevant experience may be considered.
* Eight or more years of relevant experience in NPI, manufacturing engineering, supplier development, PLM, product transfer or contract manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience moving physical products from prototype through pilot and into production.
* Experience working directly with external manufacturers or suppliers.
* Working knowledge of BOMs, routings, work instructions, engineering changes and configuration control.
* Experience with ERP/MRP and PLM or related product-data systems.
* Strong project planning, follow-through, problem-solving and written communication skills.
* Ability to work onsite in Round Rock and travel approximately 25%-35%.
* U.S. citizenship required due to the defense-related nature of the company’s work.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with technical textiles, sewn products, outdoor equipment, military products, automotive soft goods, medical textiles, inflatables or related manufacturing.
* Experience with cut-and-sew production methods, patterns, line balancing or labor standards.
* Experience with coated, laminated, printed or metallized fabrics.
* Defense, aerospace or government-contract manufacturing experience.
* Experience qualifying secondary suppliers or developing business-continuity plans.
* PMP, Lean Six Sigma, APICS or similar certification.

**Working Style**

* Hands-on and comfortable working at supplier facilities and on production floors
* Organized, practical and attentive to manufacturing details
* Able to communicate effectively with engineers, operators, supplier managers and company leadership
* Persistent in following actions through completion
* Comfortable balancing several product introductions and production issues at the same time
* Focused on building useful processes without unnecessary bureaucracy

existing_roles.description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talented team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels inspired, invested, cared for, valued, and have a strong sense of belonging.

**What You Can Expect**
-----------------------

Leads the Quality Management System (QMS) integration of acquired medical device businesses and/or products into Zimmer Biomet (ZB) network. Plans, manages and executes the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) to update, harmonize and transition the acquired site’s QMS to ZB Global Quality requirements and applicable regulations; to remediate and transfer the site’s QMS and medical device product quality documentation and records from legacy systems into ZB global enterprise IT applications; and to ensure the site obtains and/or maintains certifications and establishment registration. Partners cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Operations, Supplier Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, Servicing, IT, the Integration Management Office (IMO) and acquired-site leadership to complete integration on schedule and within budget while maintaining continuous regulatory compliance, product supply and in-process regulatory submissions.

**How You'll Create Impact**
----------------------------

* Leads cross-functional, multi-workstream QMS integration projects for newly acquired medical device businesses, from post-close planning through harmonization, documentation transfer, verification of effectiveness and integration closure.
  + Serves as the ZB Quality Integration Lead / QMS Project Leader for assigned acquisitions; accountable for the integration plan, schedule, budget, resources and deliverables.
  + Proposes corporate-wide process and issue solutions; resolves conflicts and escalates risks and roadblocks to Quality leadership and the IMO.
  + Coaches and mentors ZB and acquired-site team members on ZB Global QMS requirements; may supervise or direct team members, contractors and consultants.
  + Reviewer and approver of integration plans, gap assessments, migration protocols/reports and document-controlled forms.
  + Serves as Global SME for the QMS integration process and as site SME for multiple QMS sub-systems during transition.
  + Represents Quality in external and internal (global, site, IMO and executive) meetings, and during regulatory inspections and certification audits related to integration.
  + Strategic project planning for projects of all scale and complexity (plan, resources, budget).
* QMS Integration Planning and Project Management:
  + Translates due diligence findings into integration scope, risk-based priorities and workstreams; authors and maintains the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) per ZB global integration guidance and M&A procedures, and obtains cross-functional approval of the plan and its revisions.
  + Establishes and leads integration workstreams (e.g., Management Controls; Document & Record Controls & QMS Software; Design & Development Controls & Risk Management; Servicing; Purchasing, Production & Process Controls; CAPA / Quality Systems; Post-Market Surveillance; Regulatory and Clinical Affairs), assigning ZB and site owners, milestones and target dates.
  + Maintains detailed integration action plans, schedules and risk/issue logs (e.g., SharePoint, Smartsheet); leads recurring integration project meetings and reports status, budget, timeline, risks and roadblocks to Quality leadership, the IMO and site senior leadership.
  + Manages the integration budget and resource plan (including incremental headcount and external support) and revises the IPP when scope changes (e.g., new markets, new NPI projects, new product registrations).
* QMS Harmonization and Transition:
  + Leads gap assessments of site QMS procedures, processes and records against the ZB Global Quality Manual, global procedures (GBL/GBLW), and applicable regulations and standards; documents the harmonization approach and remediation actions.
  + Drives revision, adoption or retirement of the site Quality Manual, Quality Policy, procedures and work instructions; defines interim controls, “hybridized” processes, workstream decision forms and design control transition memoranda to maintain compliance until full adoption of global requirements.
  + Coordinates implementation of management controls, including Management Representative designation, organization charts and job descriptions, global KPIs and Global Quality Report, management review, and internal/external audit programs.
  + Establishes stakeholder-agreed cutover / go-live dates for each QMS sub-system (e.g., document control, CAPA, nonconformance, product holds, HHE/field actions, complaints, supplier controls, calibration, servicing) and ensures open legacy records are completed and closed under legacy procedures.
  + Coordinates intercompany quality agreements between the acquired site and ZB sites (e.g., complaint handling units, distribution and service centers) and contract manufacturers.

**How You'll Create Impact (cont.)**
------------------------------------

* Documentation Remediation and Transfer to ZB Enterprise Applications:
  + Plans and leads the transfer of QMS and product quality documentation and records from the acquired site’s legacy eQMS/document management system into ZB global enterprise applications (e.g., Windchill, OpenText LiveLink, WOW, Codebeamer, EtQ Reliance, iLearn, ServiceMax).

* Compliance, Effectiveness and Closure:
  + Ensures continued compliance and inspection readiness throughout the transition; initiates IE, CAPA or equivalent when gaps represent substantial noncompliance to regulatory requirements.
  + Supports site certification readiness (e.g., ISO 13485, MDSAP) and preparation for the post-integration corporate QMS audit.
  + Plans verification of effectiveness of integration activities (e.g., internal or independent QMS audit), drives closure of resulting nonconformances, and authors the IPP closure summary.
  + Captures lessons learned and continuously improves the ZB global QMS integration process, templates and playbook.

*This is not an exhaustive list of duties or functions and might not necessarily comprise all of the essential functions for purposes of the Americans with Disabilities Act.*

**What Makes You Stand Out**
----------------------------

* Expert knowledge of medical device QMS requirements: FDA 21 CFR Part 820, 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR, MDSAP and other global regulations.
* Broad working knowledge of all QMS sub-systems: document and record control, design controls, risk management, CAPA, nonconformance, complaints/MDR, HHE/field actions, supplier controls, process and software validation, calibration, servicing and post-market surveillance.
* Proven program/project management of complex, multi-workstream, cross-functional projects (scope, schedule, budget, resources, risk and change control).

* Hands-on experience with enterprise eQMS/PLM applications (e.g., Windchill, EtQ, OpenText, Codebeamer, Greenlight Guru), data migration and computer system validation.
* Strong knowledge of DHF, RMF, DMR and technical documentation content and structure.
* Ability to lead and influence without direct authority and to manage organizational change and cultural transition at acquired sites.
* Excellent executive-level communication, facilitation and status reporting.
* Sound risk-based judgement, problem solving and decision making in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.

**Your Background**

Reporting to the VP Quality Regulatory Affairs, the Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance will be tasked with ensuring Quality standards are met or exceeded in all facets of the multi-site operation. ----------------------------------

Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale.

This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.

-------------------

As **General Manager of Data Operations** at David AI, you will lead one of the most critical functions at David AI. You’ll own a major slice of our Data Factory: the engine that powers high-quality, scalable data production. You’ll lead the team responsible for building and scaling pipelines, from 0 1 experiments that unlock new model capabilities to 1 N industrialization that processes data reliably and efficiently.

**In this role, you will**
--------------------------

* Build and lead a team of Data Product Operations Leads, to spin up and scale data pipelines, from early experiments to production systems that generate high-quality audio data at scale.
* Act as a thought partner to executive leadership on how we can evolve and scale delivery capabilities in service of customer needs.
* Continuously monitor and improve pipeline health, spotting issues in sourcing, quality, or process early and owning solutions end-to-end.
* Use metrics to drive decisions, tracking throughput, quality, and cost to guide prioritization and identify where to scale or invest next.
* Work with researchers at leading AI labs to identify new model capabilities and turn them into concrete data workflows and project plans.

* Own outcomes across functions, designing systems, managing execution, unblocking bottlenecks, and ensuring delivery at both prototype and production scale.

**Your background looks like**
------------------------------

### **YOUR MISSION**

Make Nulogy's Product and Engineering organization run like a well-oiled machine, and make sure the rest of the company can see, trust, and act on what it builds. As a member of the Product Leadership Team, you will own the operating system behind how we plan, deliver, measure, and launch product. You will connect the voice of our customers and go-to-market teams to the roadmap, give leadership clear visibility into delivery and outcomes, and ensure every release lands with customers and colleagues who know exactly what changed and why it matters.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Keep the trains running on time across Product and Engineering.** Build and run an effective operating rhythm, including planning, roadmap reviews, and delivery check-ins, with one trusted view of every initiative's timeline, dependencies, and risks.
* **Raise delivery predictability.** Support and coach Product Managers and Engineering Managers to plan realistically, spot delivery risk early, and act on it.
* **Close the loop between go-to-market and Product.** Maintain a living log of product needs from new-logo and existing-customer opportunities, tied to pipeline and ARR, and track friction points across the customer lifecycle with Customer Success and Professional Services.
* **Put the right data behind product decisions.** Centralize data from our product, delivery, customer, and revenue systems so PMs and leaders can answer key questions without hunting for numbers.
* **Build trust through KPIs, reporting, and transparency.** Define core product and delivery KPIs with the Product Leadership Team, and own the dashboards and reporting that feed executive, board, and all-hands updates.
* **Align the organization around what we're building.** Make sure Product and Engineering plans are understood across GTM, Customer Success, Services, Finance, and leadership, and that every release lands through release notes, customer communications, and internal enablement.
* **Be present with customers.** Join customer visits, calls, and reviews, and bring what you hear back into planning.
* **Be a right hand to the CPO.** Drive the day-to-day of the product organization, prepare executive communication briefs, and lead special projects as they come up.

**EXPERIENCE & SKILL REQUIREMENTS**

* 8+ years in product operations, program or delivery management, product management, business operations, or a chief-of-staff-style role at a B2B SaaS company, including 3+ years working across Product and Engineering.
* A track record of running an operating rhythm and tracking delivery across multiple product and engineering teams, including coaching teams to improve predictability.
* Hands-on experience centralizing data from multiple systems into a single view
* Experience building KPIs and reporting that executives relied on for decisions.
* Strong executive communication: you've written leadership briefs, executive updates, or board materials.
* Comfortable working directly with customers, including on-site visits.
* Experience as a trusted partner to a senior leader, owning day-to-day operations and special projects.
* Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through.
* AI-first operating habits: you use AI tools daily in your own work.
* Able to travel as needed for customer visits and team offsites approximately 1-2x a quarter
* Experience in enterprise SaaS serving supply chain, manufacturing, or logistics.
* Hands-on experience with tools such as Jira and Confluence, Pendo, Salesforce or HubSpot.
* Experience running release communications or launch programs for customers and internal teams.
* Experience measuring product adoption and usage.
* A background as a Product Manager, Engineering Manager, Program Manager, or Chief of Staff to a product or engineering leader.

**COMPANY OVERVIEW**  
  
Nulogy is a manufacturing technology company driven by a vision to make life better for the people who plan, produce, and deliver the products we use every day.  
Nulogy’s Manufacturing Operating System helps manufacturers and packagers automate every stage of the production process—from inventory to quality—which reduces operating costs, increases efficiency, and boosts customer satisfaction. Hundreds of manufacturing sites around the world are powered by Nulogy, and our software also runs in the networks of world-leading brands such as Colgate-Palmolive, L’Oréal, and Procter & Gamble.  
  
Nulogy has grown rapidly over the last decade, and we are proud to be recognized with a number of awards including: Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers, Food Logistics Top 100 Software Provider, and Canada's Most Admired Corporate Culture. Nulogy has also received multiple awards for company culture, the most recent being one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers for 2024, Great Place to Work 2025 & Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for 2025.  
  
By joining Nulogy, you’ll become part of a fantastic culture of capable and motivated individuals. You’ll also join a team that is solving challenging problems every day with the potential to make a global impact.  
  
**OUR VALUES**  
**1. We put people first**  
We lead with genuine care, build strong relationships, and create space for people to grow.  
**2. We rewrite the playbook**  
We don’t wait for perfect conditions. We move, deliver, and refine, solving problems creatively as we go.  
**3. We learn up**  
We stay curious, learn from the people and experiences around us, and keep looking ahead.  
**4. We take the hot potato!**  
When something goes wrong, we don’t pass the problem along. We take ownership and work together to solve it.  
**5. We ring the bell together**  
We celebrate success as a team and recognize the people who helped make it happen.  
  
**WHY NULOGY**  
We’re solving problems that no one has been able to solve before. This is an opportunity to join a team that is transforming the way that supply chains are structured.  
  
Competitive benefits package: Group benefit plans including health, dental, and vision that start on day one—benefit premiums are fully paid by the employer; Parental leave: 100% top-up for 15 weeks for any parent of biological or adopted children; Flexible paid vacation policy; RRSP Matching Program, 401K program.  
  
**FULLY REMOTE**  
Everyone is set up with the tools and resources required to stay connected and help employees do their best work.  
  
*Nulogy embraces diversity, and we recognize the need for teams that represent a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We encourage everyone to apply.*

existing_roles.title: Vice President, Commercial Manufacturing Operations
existing_roles.description:
Vera Therapeutics is a commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on the pursuit of truth in science to transform medicine in autoimmune disease, starting with the kidney. Vera Therapeutics’ flagship commercial product is TRUTAKNATM (atacicept-vymj), a B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand *(*APRIL) inhibitor. Vera Therapeutics is evaluating multiple diseases where the reduction of autoantibodies through inhibition of BAFF and APRIL may prove clinically meaningful. Vera Therapeutics was founded in 2016 and is based in Brisbane, California. To learn more, visit www.veratx.com.

At Vera, our values are the cornerstone of our culture and guide how we work together every day. We lead with empathy, act with an owner’s mindset, demand clarity, work without fences, and execute with urgency because patients are counting on us. From how we hire and develop our people to how we advance rigorous science, we are building a team committed to transforming medicine in autoimmune diseases, starting with the kidney.

**Position Summary:**

The Vice President, Manufacturing Operations will report to the SVP Product Development and Manufacturing (PD&T) and will be responsible for leading the transition from a clinical-stage organization to an effective commercial manufacturing organization. As a key partner to the SVP PD&T, the candidate will lead and develop a best-in-class manufacturing and supply chain team that can collaboratively work across functions to enable commercial launch of our lead product into global markets. While working with internal teams, such as quality, regulatory, commercial, and finance, and external contract service providers, the individual is responsible for ensuring that the end-to-end supply chain is set up to meet the global commercial product demand with keen eye towards continuous process improvement.

**Responsibilities:**

* Leads the manufacturing and supply chain teams, providing leadership aligned with Vera values resulting in a high performing organization
* Contributes to the strategic leadership of Vera’s late-stage programs acting as a strong team player
* Participate in sales and operations planning (S&OP) and Product Development Teams representing the Product Development and Manufacturing function
* Create synergy and knowledge sharing to enable optimal production planning processes to balance supply/demand risks
* Serves as a single point of contact to manage end-to-end global supply chain and foster the needed supplier relationships to drive excellence using appropriate metrics
* Serves as a strategic thought leader to craft and manage commercial supply contracts with an eye towards life cycle extension programs
* Create, develop and manage necessary tools for end-to-end demand/supply planning
* Provide strategic direction, technical guidance, and long-range planning for late-stage programs: BLA-enabling studies through BLA submission, commercial launch, and sustaining operations
* Develop and manage department budgets and ensure fiscal responsibility for manufacturing operations
* Develop fit for purpose operational processes and systems to support supplier metrics and other tools to enable continuous improvement / process excellence
* Willingness to take on additional duties and responsibilities as assigned, and to adapt to changes in job scope as organizational needs evolve

**Qualifications:**

* Master's degree required. PhD preferred. Degree in Life Sciences or Engineering preferred
* 15+ years of relevant experience from biopharmaceutical manufacturing required.
* 5+ years of senior-level line management experience leading other leaders required
* Proven track record of creating business results
* Deep technical, operational, regulatory, strategic, and quality expertise, along with a proven track record of leading late-stage programs in innovative biotech or pharmaceutical organizations
* Experience with operating and navigating regulatory requirements including authoring and reviewing BLAs and interacting with regulatory authorities
* Solid understanding of drug development within the biopharmaceutical industry
* Experience within development and manufacturing of monoclonal antibodies or related field preferred
* Excellent interpersonal skills, collaborative leadership style
* Leads by example in recognizing and modeling Vera values
* Learning agility: ability to seek input, make connections, recognize patterns that lead to effective decision-making and action
* Proven ability to thoughtfully evaluate processes, identify opportunities for improvement and successfully execute on those plans
* Strong communication skills (oral & written); able to effectively interact with all levels internally and externally – able to tailor communications to the audience to achieve desired results
* Attention to detail with ability to move easily between hands-on work and strategic thinking
* Ability to multitask and prioritize.
* Strong leadership skills with a desire to nurture, train, and grow the existing finance group
* Demonstrated ability to influence and deliver results in a virtual (outsourced) environment

Vera Therapeutics Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer.

Vera Therapeutics is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices and we strive to provide employees with total compensation packages that are market competitive. The exact base pay offered for this role will depend on various factors, including but not limited to the candidate’s geography, qualifications, skills, and experience.

For this role, the anticipated base pay range is

$310,000 - $380,000 USD

At Vera, base pay is only one part of your total compensation package. The successful candidate will be eligible for an annual performance incentive bonus, new hire equity, and ongoing performance-based equity. Vera Therapeutics also offers various benefits offerings, including, but not limited to, medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401k match, flexible time off, and a number of paid holidays.

**Notice to Recruiters/Staffing Agencies**

Recruiters and staffing agencies should not contact Vera Therapeutics through this page. All recruitment vendors (search firms, recruitment agencies, and staffing companies) are prohibited from contacting our hiring manager(s), executive team members, or employees.

We require that all recruiters and staffing agencies have a fully executed, formal written agreement on file.

Vera Therapeutics’ receipt or acceptance of an unsolicited resume submitted by a vendor organization to this website or employee does not constitute an actual or implied contract between Vera Therapeutics and such organization and will be considered unsolicited and Vera Therapeutics will not be responsible for related fees.

**Fraud Alert**

To all candidates: your personal information and online safety are a top priority for us. At Vera Therapeutics, recruiters only direct candidates to apply through our official career page at https://veratx.com/careers/.

Recruiters will always contact you using the domain of veratx.com. We will never request payments, ask for financial account information or sensitive information like social security numbers. If you are unsure if a message is from Vera Therapeutics, please email human resources.

**CA Privacy Notice**

Applicants residing in California should review our California Privacy Notice for Employees, Job Applicants, and Contractors, which describes the categories of personal information we collect, how we use it, and your privacy rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act: https://veratx.com/ca-privacy/.

protected_roles.title: Quality Director
protected_roles.description:
**Summary**

Provides strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, ensuring that quality systems, processes, and practices support business objectives, customer requirements, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence. Establishes quality strategy, policies, objectives, and performance expectations and provides leadership across functions to drive continuous improvement, strengthen quality performance, mitigate risk, and support business growth.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, establishing priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with business and operational goals.
* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the site's Quality Management System and associated quality policies, procedures, and controls.
* Serve as the site's senior quality leader and management representative for applicable ISO 9001, AS9100, and ISO 13485 quality management systems.
* Ensure continued compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, industry, and certification requirements, including applicable FDA, ITAR, ISO, and IPC requirements and standards.
* Provide leadership for quality planning related to processes, products, customers, and business requirements, with consideration for broader corporate quality objectives.
* Establish and monitor quality metrics and performance indicators. Identify trends, risks, and systemic issues and lead actions to improve quality performance.
* Provide quality performance, risk, and improvement recommendations to site and organizational leadership.
* Lead the Material Review Board (MRB) process and provide oversight for the disposition and control of nonconforming material and product.
* Provide leadership and oversight for corrective and preventive actions, root cause analysis, and systemic problem resolution in partnership with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and other functions.
* Lead quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, improving process capability, increasing throughput, and strengthening overall operational performance.
* Drive a culture of continuous improvement and quality ownership throughout the organization.
* Provide oversight of internal and external audit activities, certification requirements, customer audits, and resulting corrective actions.
* Partner with Supply Chain and suppliers to evaluate supplier quality performance, address quality risks, and ensure supplier quality systems meet business and customer requirements.
* Oversee the calibration system and applicable preventive maintenance controls to ensure compliance and effectiveness.
* Ensure appropriate training and organizational capability related to workmanship standards, acceptance criteria, quality systems, and regulatory/customer requirements.
* Support environmental management requirements, including applicable ISO 14001 responsibilities and site environmental management activities.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Program Management, and other functions to identify and mitigate quality and operational risks and improve customer outcomes.
* Provide quality leadership and expertise in support of new products, customers, programs, processes, and business opportunities.
* Promote awareness and understanding of regulatory, customer, and quality requirements throughout the organization.
* Lead, develop, and mentor Quality leaders and team members, building organizational capability and ensuring appropriate talent development and succession planning.
* Support corporate and site Lean/6S objectives and integrate quality principles into continuous improvement initiatives.
* Support and follow all applicable Quality Management System requirements related to quality, environmental, health, safety, and security.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**Job Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Advanced knowledge of quality management systems and quality principles within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, and other applicable regulatory and customer quality requirements.
* Working knowledge of FDA, ITAR, IPC, and applicable electronics manufacturing standards and requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to translate business objectives into quality strategies, priorities, metrics, and improvement initiatives.
* Strong knowledge of corrective action, root cause analysis, risk management, process improvement, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to analyze quality and operational data, identify trends and systemic risks, and develop effective corrective and preventive strategies.
* Strong business acumen with the ability to balance quality, customer, operational, financial, and business considerations.
* Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and drive results across functions without relying solely on direct authority.
* Strong leadership and organizational capability, including experience building, developing, and leading professional and technical teams.
* Ability to communicate effectively with customers, regulatory bodies, auditors, suppliers, and senior leadership.
* Strong written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and applicable electronic manufacturing and quality systems.

**Experience/Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations, or a related technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible quality, engineering, or manufacturing experience, including significant leadership responsibility.
* Demonstrated experience leading a quality organization within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Experience managing multiple concurrent technical, quality, and operational priorities.
* Demonstrated experience influencing cross-functional leaders and driving organization-wide quality and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience interacting with customers, auditors, regulatory organizations, and senior business leadership.
* Demonstrated balance of strategic thinking, strong analytical capability, and effective execution.
* Strong business judgment, attention to detail, and written and verbal communication skills.

**Due to ITAR and / or CUI compliance, this position requires candidates to be a U.S. Citizen.**

Benefits Offered: Comprehensive benefit package including medical, dental and vision coverage; company-paid basic life/AD&D insurance, short-term and long-term disability insurance; voluntary supplemental insurances, flexible spending accounts and employee assistance program (EAP). Sick Leave, Vacation Time, and company-paid Holidays are also provided as paid time off. NEOTech also provides a 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan option with a company match.

NEOTech is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

NEOTech has a long-standing commitment to maintaining a safe, quality-oriented and productive work environment. We also want all employees to perform their duties safely and efficiently, in a manner that protects their interests and those of their co-workers. We recognize that alcohol and drug abuse pose a threat to the health and safety of NEOTech employees and to the security of the Company’s equipment and facilities. For these reasons, NEOTech is committed to the elimination of drug and alcohol use and abuse in the workplace. Candidates being considered for hire must pass a pre-employment background check and drug test which include screening for illegal drugs and marijuana.

protected_roles.description:
About Us:

### ***Specialized Care for the Patients Who Need It Most.***

NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals (NPH) is dedicated to providing unparalleled service to our patients, team members, physicians, and families. We dare to do things differently, bringing together compassionate care, specialized expertise, and an interdisciplinary approach to meet the unique needs of those we serve. It is this commitment that distinguishes NPH as the healthcare provider of choice.

As a national leader in behavioral healthcare, NPH specializes in caring for patients with acute psychiatric and complex medical needs. Our hospitals provide patient-centered care through an interdisciplinary, multi-specialty approach, ensuring our patients receive the specialized support they need when they need it most.

With locations in Indiana, Michigan, Texas, Ohio, and Arizona, we are expanding access to our unique model of care across the United States. Join NPH and become part of a team that is daring to do things differently and making a lasting difference in the lives of our patients, families, and communities every day.

Overview:

NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals is looking for a Director of Quality and Risk at our **Huber Heights, OH** location. NPH is the national leader in providing medical and neurobehavioral care to patients in acute psychiatric distress. You will be joining a team of rock star staff who provide exceptional, patient-centered care and understand our patients are always our number one priority! The Director of Quality supports the implementation and monitoring of the quality assurance measurements and audits, and assists in improving patient safety processes throughout the hospital through coordinating and engaging in activities to proactively promote implementation of evidence based best practices and resolve deficiencies; plans, develops, and directs system activities and protocols across NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals; helps to prepare NPH facilities for surveys by accrediting and licensing agencies; serves as a resource to all departments and personnel.

**Benefits of joining NPH as a Director of Quality and Risk**

* Competitive pay rates
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* NPH 401(k) plan with up to 4% Company match
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Programs
* Generous PTO and Time Off Policy
* Special tuition offers through Capella University
* Work/life balance with great professional growth opportunities
* Employee Discounts through LifeMart

Responsibilities:

* Implements and monitors quality goals and objectives to measure the organization’s processes and outcomes while administering programs that focus on improved outcomes of patient care or patient safety.
* Interacts with physicians, nurses, department managers, supervisors, and any/all other staff members to provide resource information and identify new opportunities to improve service and reduce costs.
* Generates effectual quality related policies and procedures for the department and hospital that ensures compliance with JC, OSHA, CDC, CMS and other county, state, and federal regulatory agencies.
* Prepares reports, presentations and statistical data that go to the Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement Committee Meetings, facility's administration and other committees as needed. Analyzes data to identify trends and resource utilization for use in optimizing compliance.
* Assists with the annual assessment of the quality control programs from the prior year activities.
* Investigates incidents within the facility and coordinates with the Corporate Quality team to complete the root cause analysis and develop action plans to prevent incidents in the future.
* Establish a structure to ensure that patient care activities are addressed in a coordinated manner involving quality improvement.
* Prepares the agenda for the Quality Council Committee meetings and holds regularly scheduled meetings.
* Provides educational offerings for orientation and on-going in-services.
* Performs mortality reviews in conjunction with the mortality committee and holds regularly scheduled mortality committee meetings.
* Ensures all staff receive proper education on new or revised state and/ or federal regulations or Joint Commission standards.
* Participates in Multi-disciplinary patient centered case conferences, as appropriate.
* Assess and evaluate patients with infections and monitor patient outcomes on an ongoing basis.
* Initiates follow-up on employee/patient exposures to communicable diseases.
* Participates in root-cause analysis, sentinel events, adverse events and identifies trends as directed by regulation. Recommends ways to redesign systems for improvements if needed.
* Oversee Patient Advocacy program.
* Establishes/maintains good relationships with COO, CEO and DON’s and department leaders to promote a cooperative and constructive environment for improvement.
* Promote “Quality is everyone’s business” to gain support, understanding and ownership among staff.
* Other duties as may be assigned.
* Complies with hospital expectations regarding ethical behavior and standards of conduct.
* Complies with federal and hospital requirements in the areas of protected health information & patient privacy.
* Understands and adheres to NPH’s compliance standards as they appear in NPH’s Corporate Compliance Policy, Code of Conduct and Conflict of Interest Policy.
* Keeps abreast of all pertinent federal, state and hospital regulations, laws and policies as they presently exist and as they change or are modified.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's Degree in healthcare field or pertinent program required. Master's Degree preferred.
* 3+ years of relevant healthcare quality and risk management experience. Prior leadership experience preferred.
* Excellent verbal communication skills necessary in order present quality reports.
* Maintain effective contacts with a variety of Hospital Personnel.
* Professional knowledge of clinical practice, leadership, performance improvement and research statistics in order to conduct surveillance and prepare related reports at a level normally acquired through the completion of a Bachelor’s degree in related field.

This position is incentive eligible.  
  
  

Do you have the career opportunities as a Group Quality Director you want with your current employer? We have an exciting opportunity for you to join HCA Laboratory Services which is part of the nation's leading provider of healthcare services, HCA Healthcare.

Travel is Required. You will Support 5- Divisions. Must Reside in Utah, Idaho, Nevada, North Carolina, Virginia, Alaska or in the Nashville, TN area.

Job Summary and Qualifications

The Group Quality Director is responsible for implementation of the Laboratory Service Line quality and performance improvement programs for our National Group. This position applies quality and performance improvement approaches to identify and quantify improvement opportunities, facilitate and organization process improvement efforts, drive improvement, and measure outcomes. This role supervises Quality Coordinators in assigned divisions. You will be responsible for laboratory regulatory agency accreditation preparedness, tracking and reporting of specific information; auditing and analysis of processes and systems; statistical analysis of data; formulation of recommendations; and creation of written and verbal reports. The position also requires skills for developing and presenting related training programs for laboratory colleagues and for preparing presentations to and for management.

In This Role You Will:

* Deploy the laboratory clinical quality infrastructure across the National Group divisions.
* Partner with leaders to identify and coordinate implementation of continual improvement projects to improve quality performance.
* Facilitate the growth of vision of laboratory quality and performance, including the dissemination of "best practices" across the country.
* Lead regional process improvement initiatives, provide feedback on standardization opportunities and evaluate success through pre-established criteria.
* Assist with appropriate and timely response to Serious Patient Adverse Events (SPAE)s that involve laboratory operations.
* Lead proactive laboratory quality and safety activities to create hospital laboratories that are highly reliable as reflected in reduced errors, elimination of unsafe processes and increase involvement of staff and pathology medical directors toward a culture of safety.
* Contribute to the achievement of laboratory business and financial goals through optimal division and group performance in quality and patient safety.
* Interface with appropriate personnel at HCA to leverage corporate resources, programs, tools and methodologies for benefit of hospital laboratories.
* Collaborate with and support hospital quality, risk, safety and infection prevention leaders to achieve top ranking in national and state publicly reported data initiatives.
* Participate in regular analysis of laboratory quality and risk performance data, and plan steps for ongoing improvement.
* Work with Corporate and Division medical leaders to support data analysis, reporting, process and outcomes improvement.
* Contribute to ongoing enhancement of enterprise quality reporting methods and dashboards.
* Continuously monitor and evaluate quality outcomes across the group and division, while noting trends and identifying and prioritizing opportunities to improve.
* Assist divisions in building a proactive quality department by implementing processes to support accreditation and regulatory inspections.
* Facilitate and/or lead process improvement teams as needed to achieve quality improvement goals.
* Serve as a regulatory resource regarding state and federal regulations and standards, including but not limited to CMS, CLIA, CAP, and TJC.
* Demonstrate personal responsibility for professional development, and promoting and supporting laboratory quality leaders and division data analysts.
* Promote a culture that is positive, values individual strengths, takes risks and is committed to optimal patient care and compliance with standards.
* Attend HCA-mandated training and meeting all ethics and compliance standards and requirements.
* Develop and implement projects as directed by AVP, Quality and CLO.

What Qualifications You Will Need:

* Bachelor's degree in a clinical laboratory, chemical, biological science or related field is required.
* Master's degree in a related field is preferred.
* 3+ years of experience in quality improvement is required.
* 1+ years of experience in clinical laboratory is preferred.
* Management experience is preferred.
* Previous experience within a multi-facility environment is preferred.
* Clinical licensure, Laboratory Medical Technology or RN is preferred.
* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) is preferred.

##### **Benefits**

Work from Home, offers a total rewards package that supports the health, life, career and retirement of our colleagues. The available plans and programs include:

* **Comprehensive benefits** for medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, behavioral health and telemedicine services
* **Wellbeing support,** including free counseling and referral services
* **Time away from work** programs for paid time off, paid family leave, long- and short-term disability coverage and leaves of absence

* **Education support** through tuition assistance, student loan assistance, certification support, dependent scholarships and a partnership with Galen College of Nursing
* **Additional benefits** for fertility and family building, adoption assistance, life insurance, supplemental health protection plans, auto and home insurance, legal counseling, identity theft protection and consumer discounts

Learn more about Employee Benefits

Founded in 1982 as Joliet Area Community Hospice, Lightways Hospice and Serious Illness Care is an independent, nonprofit healthcare provider licensed in 11 counties in northwest Illinois. We provide exceptional serious illness care, hospice care and grief support for adults and children.

The majority of our direct patient care is in the field with Lightways team members providing care in the home, nursing facility or assisted living facility. We also have a 24-bed inpatient unit in Joliet. Non-clinical staff are based out of our Joliet administrative offices.

**Director of Quality and Compliance**

The Director of Quality & Compliance provides administrative oversight for Quality, Compliance, Medical Records, and Risk Management functions, while also serving as the organization’s designated Compliance Officer.

This role delivers strategic and operational leadership for the Lightways Quality Assessment & Performance Improvement (QAPI) program, regulatory compliance, accreditation readiness, clinical education, and risk management. The Director is responsible for developing, implementing, and evaluating robust systems that promote safety, regulatory adherence, and high-quality care across all organizational operations.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Reference, research, report, track, and monitor compliance and quality-related data.
* Develop, implement, and evaluate strategies for quality assurance, performance improvement, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
* Create and maintain the organization’s annual Quality and Compliance Plans and Reports.
* Lead quarterly Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) meetings.
* Review Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) survey data, complaints, and incident reports to inform improvement strategies.
* Develop and deliver education, policies, and process improvements to promote accurate, timely, and compliant clinical documentation across the organization.

  

**Education/Experience:**

* Master's degree in healthcare or related field (required)
* Management experience with hospice and/or palliative care experience preferred.
* Certification in a specialist area preferred; (e.g. Hospice and Palliative Nursing (CHPN), Pediatrics or Geriatrics)

  

**Benefits:**

* 401(k) matching
* Health Insurance
* Dental Insurance
* Vision Insurance
* Personal Time Off
* Holiday Paid

We’re excited to find individuals who are eager to be part of a team that’s driving global impact through innovation, sustainability, and purpose.
  
  
**Location:** 715 Fountain Avenue, Lancaster, PA 17601
  
  
Lead a High-Performing Manufacturing Operation and Drive Operational Excellence
  
Are you a hands-on manufacturing leader who thrives on building strong teams, improving performance, and creating a culture of accountability and continuous improvement? We are seeking a Plant Manager to lead all aspects of site operations, including safety, quality, delivery, cost, maintenance, and employee development.
  
This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact in a close-knit manufacturing environment where leadership matters, employee engagement is valued, and continuous improvement is part of the culture. We're looking for a servant leader who is willing to roll up their sleeves, develop people, challenge the status quo, and drive measurable business results.

* Safety performance and employee engagement
* Product quality and customer satisfaction
* On-time delivery and schedule attainment
* Cost control and operational efficiency
* Maintenance and facility reliability

* Lead daily plant operations to ensure safety, quality, delivery, and cost targets are achieved.
* Develop, coach, and mentor supervisors and department leaders.
* Foster a culture built on accountability, trust, teamwork, and servant leadership.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives utilizing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 6S, and other operational excellence tools.

* Ensure maintenance programs support operational reliability and uptime.

* Demonstrated track record of improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost metrics.
* Experience working with ERP/MRP systems for production scheduling, inventory, and shop floor operations.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing labor, maintenance, and capital budgets.

Apply today and become the leader who drives the next chapter of operational excellence.

Operations & Production

* Direct day-to-day manufacturing, fabrication, assembly, and shipping activities to meet customer commitments
* Work with production scheduling and Supply Chain to balance capacity, labor, and material availability

People Leadership

* Partner with Human Resources on hiring, onboarding, employee relations, performance management, and engagement

* Build a positive, inclusive culture where employees feel safe, respected, and invested in the site’s success

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Work closely with Engineering on product design, manufacturability, and technical issues

PuraGraft represents the leading manufacturers of biomaterial solutions for bone and tissue regeneration. No single material can suit all medical requirements and indications. However, through PuraGraft® you have access to the widest choices of products.

At Young Innovations, we foster a dynamic environment where team members make an impact every day as part of a collaborative, inclusive culture. Together, we serve the dental profession and their patients, united in our mission of achieving a Lifetime of Oral Health™

We embrace diverse perspectives and encourage bold thinking, challenging traditional approaches with a bias for action. Whether you’re looking to expand your skills or grow your career, Young is here to support your goals and continuous learning. At Young, YOU are at the core of what we do.

**Position Overview:**

Reporting to the VP Quality Regulatory Affairs, the Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance will be tasked with ensuring Quality standards are met or exceeded in all facets of the multi-site operation. He/she will partner internally in the development and implementation of new or adjusted quality standards, policies, and procedures, as required at Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ.

**You’ll like this role if:**

* You enjoy leading a team, solving complex quality challenges, and turning data into practical improvements. You take ownership of compliance and thrive in a hands-on role supporting quality standards across multiple sites.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here:**

* Medium sized company – not too big, not too small – just enough to get things done and see your impact.
* Did we say benefits? Full medical, dental, vision, 401k, parental leave, paid holidays, paid time off, short & long term disability insurance, employee assistance program, and more!
* Lead and inspire a dedicated team, build meaningful relationships, and help your employees grow and succeed.

**Who you’ll work with:**

* You’ll report to the VP of Quality & Regulatory Affairs and lead Quality Associates supporting our Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ operations.
* You’ll partner closely with QRA, Sourcing, Distribution, and Production teams to strengthen quality systems and drive continuous improvement.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Act as the site’s Sr. Quality and Compliance Leader, and when necessary, as the site’s Designated Management Representative to ensure compliance with all regulatory, corporate and facility requirements.
* Ensure compliance of two sites.
* Ensure outstanding Quality System performance via monitoring and measuring of process performance, and driving any appropriate action, including issuing and follow-up on activities required for sourcing, warehousing, and distributing pharmaceuticals.
* Supervise & Manage Quality Associates and develop culture of collaboration and cross-functional success within the department and business.
* Reviews and monitors Quality metrics and reports trends, to determine if there is a need to escalate issues to the management.
* Perform, review and monitor the Quality Management processes which include but is not limited to:
  + Ensure compliance with FDA, DEA and BOP requirements, including DSCSA traceability of pharmaceuticals.
  + Oversee Regulatory activities associated with distribution licensing, drug distribution reports, and permits for warehousing and distribution of controlled substances.
  + inspection and product release, label approval, calibration, warehousing controls, record retention, document control, training, control of non-conforming product, quarantined Products, control of access and drugs storage, including temperature monitoring.
  + Host and manage internal and external audits. Ensure the site’s readiness for assessments and lead implementation of corrective actions.
  + Effectively assess processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
  + Review, Analyze and Report Statistical findings through critical thought and storytelling of key findings and opportunities to all levels within a matrixed organization.
  + Partner with other departments to identify critical to quality metrics, and support the operationalization of monitoring and management to deliver improved performance across processes.
  + Create effective and compelling visual materials/presentations that support the process/product improvement impact to the organization and adequately represent the impact to quality, cost and time.
  + Define, track, and monitor key success measures associated with Quality Management Systems. Successfully deploy and support change management and appropriate training plans.
* Manage document control functions, including creation, review, and approval of procedures, work instructions and all other documentation for the Quality System.
* Manage the complaint handling system, including trending and review to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the training of the Site, by maintaining the training log, tracking training completion of training by site personnel, creating training content and hosting group training as needed.
* Develop and host the Quarterly Management Review
* Manage the Recall process, from notification, tracking responses & expenses, reporting, and closure.
* Develop, refine, and/or maintain quality standards, policies, and procedures for the facility, including identifying, recommending, and fully implementing changes, in partnership with corporate QRA and local operations teams. Other duties as assigned

**What You’ll Bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in technical field.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience managing manufacturing and/or distribution of pharmaceuticals.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience having direct responsibility for managing a Quality group.
* Direct experience managing FDA or DEA Inspections.
* Demonstrated proficiency in verbal and written communication in English, with the ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and professionally across all levels of the organization.

**Travel Requirements**

* Up to 15%

**Work Environment:**

**Office Environment**

This position is based in an office environment and is primarily sedentary in nature. It requires regular use of standard office equipment, including computers, phones, photocopiers, scanners, filing cabinets, and fax machines. Some roles may involve wearing a headset and sustained computer use for 8 or more hours per day. Employees may be required to sit, stand, or walk for extended periods, and occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

**Manufacturing/Distribution Environment**

This position operates in a manufacturing plant environment. The role routinely involves working around machinery, equipment, and moving mechanical parts. The facility may be subject to varying temperatures, loud noise levels, and airborne particles such as dust or chemical fumes, depending on the area of the plant. This role may require periods of standing, sitting, or walking throughout the workday. Occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, control, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk. Hearing abilities required for this environment include being able to clearly hear and respond to audible alarms, production equipment, forklifts, and other machinery to maintain a safe work environment. Individuals must be able to distinguish and understand verbal communication including instructions, safety warnings, and team discussions, sometimes in an environment with moderate to high background noise.

------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

**About our Data Operations team**
----------------------------------

Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale.

This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.

You’ll lead the team responsible for building and scaling pipelines, from 0 1 experiments that unlock new model capabilities to 1 N industrialization that processes data reliably and efficiently.

--------------------------

* Build and lead a team of Data Product Operations Leads, to spin up and scale data pipelines, from early experiments to production systems that generate high-quality audio data at scale.
* Act as a thought partner to executive leadership on how we can evolve and scale delivery capabilities in service of customer needs.

* Prior experience scaling large-scale operational efforts at high-growth startups or fast-paced companies.

* Background in CS, industrial engineering, or similar.

* Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.

From how we hire and develop our people to how we advance rigorous science, we are building a team committed to transforming medicine in autoimmune diseases, starting with the kidney.

**Position Summary:**

The Vice President, Manufacturing Operations will report to the SVP Product Development and Manufacturing (PD&T) and will be responsible for leading the transition from a clinical-stage organization to an effective commercial manufacturing organization. As a key partner to the SVP PD&T, the candidate will lead and develop a best-in-class manufacturing and supply chain team that can collaboratively work across functions to enable commercial launch of our lead product into global markets. While working with internal teams, such as quality, regulatory, commercial, and finance, and external contract service providers, the individual is responsible for ensuring that the end-to-end supply chain is set up to meet the global commercial product demand with keen eye towards continuous process improvement.

**Responsibilities:**

* Leads the manufacturing and supply chain teams, providing leadership aligned with Vera values resulting in a high performing organization
* Contributes to the strategic leadership of Vera’s late-stage programs acting as a strong team player
* Participate in sales and operations planning (S&OP) and Product Development Teams representing the Product Development and Manufacturing function
* Create synergy and knowledge sharing to enable optimal production planning processes to balance supply/demand risks
* Serves as a single point of contact to manage end-to-end global supply chain and foster the needed supplier relationships to drive excellence using appropriate metrics
* Serves as a strategic thought leader to craft and manage commercial supply contracts with an eye towards life cycle extension programs
* Create, develop and manage necessary tools for end-to-end demand/supply planning
* Provide strategic direction, technical guidance, and long-range planning for late-stage programs: BLA-enabling studies through BLA submission, commercial launch, and sustaining operations
* Develop and manage department budgets and ensure fiscal responsibility for manufacturing operations
* Develop fit for purpose operational processes and systems to support supplier metrics and other tools to enable continuous improvement / process excellence
* Willingness to take on additional duties and responsibilities as assigned, and to adapt to changes in job scope as organizational needs evolve

**Qualifications:**

* Master's degree required. PhD preferred. Degree in Life Sciences or Engineering preferred
* 15+ years of relevant experience from biopharmaceutical manufacturing required.
* 5+ years of senior-level line management experience leading other leaders required
* Proven track record of creating business results
* Deep technical, operational, regulatory, strategic, and quality expertise, along with a proven track record of leading late-stage programs in innovative biotech or pharmaceutical organizations
* Experience with operating and navigating regulatory requirements including authoring and reviewing BLAs and interacting with regulatory authorities
* Solid understanding of drug development within the biopharmaceutical industry
* Experience within development and manufacturing of monoclonal antibodies or related field preferred
* Excellent interpersonal skills, collaborative leadership style
* Leads by example in recognizing and modeling Vera values
* Learning agility: ability to seek input, make connections, recognize patterns that lead to effective decision-making and action
* Proven ability to thoughtfully evaluate processes, identify opportunities for improvement and successfully execute on those plans
* Strong communication skills (oral & written); able to effectively interact with all levels internally and externally – able to tailor communications to the audience to achieve desired results
* Attention to detail with ability to move easily between hands-on work and strategic thinking
* Ability to multitask and prioritize.
* Strong leadership skills with a desire to nurture, train, and grow the existing finance group
* Demonstrated ability to influence and deliver results in a virtual (outsourced) environment
